2.3.e: A righteous man shall seek to dwell in a village where fuel, water, fodder, sacred fuel, Kuśa grass, and garlands are plentiful, access to which is easy, where many rich people dwell, which abounds in industrious people, where Āryans form the majority, and which is not easily entered by robbers.

2.3.s: udapānodake grāme brāhmaṇo vṛṣalīpatiḥ | uṣitvā dvādaśa samāḥ śūdrasādharmyam ṛcchati |
2.3.d: उदपानोदके ग्रामे ब्राह्मणो वृषलीपतिः । उषित्वा द्वादश समाः शूद्रसाधर्म्यम् ऋच्छति ।
2.3.e: 'A Brāhmaṇa who, having wedded a wife of the Śūdra caste and dwells during twelve years in a village where water (is obtainable) from wells only, becomes equal to a Śūdra.'

2.3.s: purareṇukuṇṭhitaśarīras tatparipurṇanetravadanaś ca | nagare vasan suniyatātmā siddhim avāpsyatīti na tad asti |
2.3.d: पुररेणुकुण्ठितशरीरस् तत्परिपुर्णनेत्रवदनश् च । नगरे वसन् सुनियतात्मा सिद्धिम् अवाप्स्यतीति न तद् अस्ति ।
2.3.e: (If you say that) he who lives in a town and whose body is covered with the dust, (raised) by others, and whose eyes and mouth are filled with it, will obtain salvation, if he restrains himself, (I declare that) that is impossible.

2.3.s: rathāśvagajadhānyānāṃ gavāṃ caiva rajaḥ śubham | apraśastaṃ samūhanyāḥ śvājāvikharavāsasām |
2.3.d: रथाश्वगजधान्यानां गवां चैव रजः शुभम् । अप्रशस्तं समूहन्याः श्वाजाविखरवाससाम् ।
2.3.e: 'The dust raised by carriages, horses, elephants, and cows, and (that which comes) from grain is pure, blamed is (that raised) by a broom, goats, sheep, donkeys, and garments.'

2.3.s: pūjyān pūjayet |
2.3.d: पूज्यान् पूजयेत् ।
2.3.e: Let him honour those who are worthy of honour.

2.3.s: ṛṣividvannṛpavaramātulaśvaśurartvijaḥ | ete 'rghyāḥ śāstravihitāḥ smṛtāḥ kālavibhāgaśaḥ |
2.3.d: ऋषिविद्वन्नृपवरमातुलश्वशुरर्त्विजः । एते ऽर्घ्याः शास्त्रविहिताः स्मृताः कालविभागशः ।
2.3.e: 'A Ri shi, a learned man, a king, a bride-groom, a maternal uncle, a father-in-law, and an officiating priest are mentioned in the Sm ri ti as worthy of the honey-mixture at certain times and occasions.'

2.3.s: ṛṣividvannṛpāḥ prāptāḥ kriyārambhe varartvijau | mātulaśvaśurau pūjyau saṃvatsaragatāgatau || iti |
2.3.d: ऋषिविद्वन्नृपाः प्राप्ताः क्रियारम्भे वरर्त्विजौ । मातुलश्वशुरौ पूज्यौ संवत्सरगतागतौ ॥ इति ।
2.3.e: 'A Ri shi, a learned man, and a king must be honoured whenever they come, a bridegroom and a priest at the beginning of the religious rites, a maternal uncle and a father-in-law when a year has elapsed since their last visit.'

2.3.s: agnyagāre gavāṃ madhye brāhmaṇānāṃ ca saṃnidhau | svādhyāye bhojane caiva dakṣiṇaṃ bāhum uddharet |
2.3.d: अग्न्यगारे गवां मध्ये ब्राह्मणानां च संनिधौ । स्वाध्याये भोजने चैव दक्षिणं बाहुम् उद्धरेत् ।
2.3.e: 'Let him raise his right arm on (entering) the place where the sacred fire is kept, in the midst of a herd of cows, in the presence of Brāhmaṇas, at the daily recitation of the Veda, and at dinner.'

2.3.s: uttaraṃ vāsaḥ kartavyaṃ pañcasv eteṣu karmasu | svādhyāyotsargadāneṣu bhojanācāmayos tathā |
2.3.d: उत्तरं वासः कर्तव्यं पञ्चस्व् एतेषु कर्मसु । स्वाध्यायोत्सर्गदानेषु भोजनाचामयोस् तथा ।
2.3.e: 'An upper garment must be worn on the following five occasions: during the daily study, during the evacuation (of excrements), when one bestows gifts, at dinner, and while one sips water.'

2.3.s: havanaṃ bhojanaṃ dānam upahāraḥ pratigrahaḥ | bahirjānu na kāryāṇi tadvad ācamanaṃ smṛtam |
2.3.d: हवनं भोजनं दानम् उपहारः प्रतिग्रहः । बहिर्जानु न कार्याणि तद्वद् आचमनं स्मृतम् ।
2.3.e: 'While one offers oblations in the fire, while one dines, bestows gifts, offers (food to deities or Gurus), and accepts presents, (the right hand) must be placed between the knees.'

2.3.s: anne śritāni bhūtāni annaṃ prāṇam iti śrutiḥ | tasmād annaṃ pradātavyam annaṃ hi paramaṃ haviḥ |
2.3.d: अन्ने श्रितानि भूतानि अन्नं प्राणम् इति श्रुतिः । तस्माद् अन्नं प्रदातव्यम् अन्नं हि परमं हविः ।
2.3.e: 'The revealed texts declare, that the creatures depend on food, food is life; therefore gifts of food must be made. Food is the most excellent of sacrificial viands.'

2.3.s: hutena śāmyate pāpaṃ hutam annena śāmyati | annaṃ dakṣiṇayā śāntim upayātīti na śrutiḥ | upayātīti naḥ śrutir iti |
2.3.d: हुतेन शाम्यते पापं हुतम् अन्नेन शाम्यति । अन्नं दक्षिणया शान्तिम् उपयातीति न श्रुतिः । उपयातीति नः श्रुतिर् इति ।
2.3.e: 'Sin is removed by burnt offerings, burnt oblations are surpassed by (gifts of) food, and gifts of food by kind speeches. That (is declared) to us in the revealed texts.'

2.4.s: athātaḥ saṃdhyopāsanavidhiṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ |
2.4.d: अथातः संध्योपासनविधिं व्याख्यास्यामः ।
2.4.e: Now, therefore, we will declare the rule for (performing) the twilight devotions.

2.4.s: tīrthaṃ gatvāprayato 'bhiṣiktaḥ prayato vānabhiṣiktaḥprakṣālitapādapāṇir apa ācamya surabhimatyābliṅgābhirvāruṇībhir hiraṇyavarṇābhiḥ pāvamānībhir vyāhṛtibhir anyaiś capavitrair ātmānaṃ prokṣya prayato bhavati |
2.4.d: तीर्थं गत्वाप्रयतो ऽभिषिक्तः प्रयतो वानभिषिक्तःप्रक्षालितपादपाणिर् अप आचम्य सुरभिमत्याब्लिङ्गाभिर्वारुणीभिर् हिरण्यवर्णाभिः पावमानीभिर् व्याहृतिभिर् अन्यैश् चपवित्रैर् आत्मानं प्रोक्ष्य प्रयतो भवति ।
2.4.e: Going to a (sacred) bathing-place, he shall bathe, in case he is impure; in case he is pure, he may, optionally, omit the bath. (But in either case) he shall wash his feet and hands. Sipping water and sprinkling himself, while he recites the (Rik-verses) containing the word Surabhi, the Abliṅgas, those addressed to Varuṇa, the Hiraṇyavarṇas, the Pāvamānīs, the (sacred syllables called) Vyāh ri tis, and other purificatory (texts), he becomes pure (and fit to perform the twilight devotions).

2.4.s: athāpy udāharanti | apovagāhanaṃ apo 'vagāhanaṃ snānaṃ vihitaṃ sārvavarṇikam | mantravatprokṣaṇaṃ cāpi dvijātīnāṃ viśiṣyate || iti |
2.4.d: अथाप्य् उदाहरन्ति । अपोवगाहनं अपो ऽवगाहनं स्नानं विहितं सार्ववर्णिकम् । मन्त्रवत्प्रोक्षणं चापि द्विजातीनां विशिष्यते ॥ इति ।
2.4.e: Now they quote also (the following verse): 'Submersion in water (and) bathing are prescribed for all the (four) castes. But sprinkling (water over the body), while Mantras (are being recited), is the particular (duty) of the twice-born.'

2.4.s: sarvakarmaṇāṃ caivārambheṣu prāk saṃdhyopāsanakālāccaitenaiva pavitrasamūhenātmānaṃ prokṣya prayato bhavati |
2.4.d: सर्वकर्मणां चैवारम्भेषु प्राक् संध्योपासनकालाच्चैतेनैव पवित्रसमूहेनात्मानं प्रोक्ष्य प्रयतो भवति ।
2.4.e: He who sprinkles himself (with water) at the beginning of any sacred rite,--before the time of the twilight devotions,--while reciting that same collection of purificatory (texts), becomes pure.

2.4.s: athāpy udāharanti | darbheṣv āsīno darbhān dhārayamāṇaḥsodakena pāṇinā pratyaṅmukhaḥ sāvitrīṃ sahasrakṛtva āvartayet |
2.4.d: अथाप्य् उदाहरन्ति । दर्भेष्व् आसीनो दर्भान् धारयमाणःसोदकेन पाणिना प्रत्यङ्मुखः सावित्रीं सहस्रकृत्व आवर्तयेत् ।
2.4.e: Now they quote also (the following rules): Seated, with his face to the west, on Darbha grass and holding Darbha blades in his (right) hand, which is filled with water, he shall repeat the Sāvitrī one thousand times;

2.4.s: prāṇāyāmaśo vā śatakṛtvaḥ |
2.4.d: प्राणायामशो वा शतकृत्वः ।
2.4.e: Or (he may recite the verse) one hundred times, suppressing his breath;

2.4.s: ubhayataḥpraṇavāṃ sasaptavyāhṛtikāṃ manasā vā daśakṛtvaḥ |
2.4.d: उभयतःप्रणवां ससप्तव्याहृतिकां मनसा वा दशकृत्वः ।
2.4.e: Or mentally ten times, adding the syllable Om at the beginning and at the end and the seven Vyāh ri tis.

2.4.s: tribhiś ca prāṇāyāmais tānto brahmahṛdayena |
2.4.d: त्रिभिश् च प्राणायामैस् तान्तो ब्रह्महृदयेन ।
2.4.e: And if he is tired by three suppressions of his breath (performed) with (the recitation of) the (Anuvāka called) Brahmah ri daya (the heart of Brahman, then let him repeat the Sāvitrī).

2.4.s: vāruṇībhyāṃ rātrim upatiṣṭhate | imaṃ me varuṇa | tat tvā yāmīti | dvābhyām |
2.4.d: वारुणीभ्यां रात्रिम् उपतिष्ठते । इमं मे वरुण । तत् त्वा यामीति । द्वाभ्याम् ।
2.4.e: In the evening he worships (the sun) with the two (verses) addressed to Varuṇa, 'Hear this my call, O Varuṇa,' and 'Therefore I go to thee.'

2.4.s: evam eva prātaḥ prāṅmukhas tiṣṭhan |
2.4.d: एवम् एव प्रातः प्राङ्मुखस् तिष्ठन् ।
2.4.e: The same (rules apply to the twilight devotion) in the morning, (but the worshipper) shall face the east and stand upright.

2.4.s: maitrībhyām ahar upatiṣṭhate | mitrasya carṣaṇīdhṛtaḥ | mitrojanān yātayatīti | dvābhyām |
2.4.d: मैत्रीभ्याम् अहर् उपतिष्ठते । मित्रस्य चर्षणीधृतः । मित्रोजनान् यातयतीति । द्वाभ्याम् ।
2.4.e: In the day-time he worships (the sun) with the two (verses) addressed to Mitra, 'The glory of Mitra, who supports men,' and 'Mitra causes men to join.'

2.4.s: supūrvām api pūrvām upakramyodita āditye samāpnuyāt |
2.4.d: सुपूर्वाम् अपि पूर्वाम् उपक्रम्योदित आदित्ये समाप्नुयात् ।
2.4.e: Let him begin (the twilight devotion) in the morning very early, and finish it when the sun has risen.

2.4.s: anastamita upakramya supaścād api paścimām |
2.4.d: अनस्तमित उपक्रम्य सुपश्चाद् अपि पश्चिमाम् ।
2.4.e: Let him begin (the twilight devotion) in the evening, when (the sun) has set, (and finish it) very soon after (the appearance of the stars);

2.4.s: saṃdhyayoś ca saṃpattāv ahorātrayoś ca saṃtatyai |
2.4.d: संध्ययोश् च संपत्ताव् अहोरात्रयोश् च संतत्यै ।
2.4.e: And the complete observance of the twilight devotions (produces as its reward) an uninterrupted succession of days and nights.

2.4.s: api cātra prajāpatigītau ślokau bhavataḥ | anāgatāṃ tu ye pūrvām anatītāṃ tu paścimām | saṃdhyāṃ nopāsate viprāḥ kathaṃ te brāhmaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ | sāyaṃ prātaḥ sadā saṃdhyāṃ ye viprā no upāsate | kāmaṃ tān dhārmiko rājā śūdrakarmasu yojayed || iti |
2.4.d: अपि चात्र प्रजापतिगीतौ श्लोकौ भवतः । अनागतां तु ये पूर्वाम् अनतीतां तु पश्चिमाम् । संध्यां नोपासते विप्राः कथं ते ब्राह्मणाः स्मृताः । सायं प्रातः सदा संध्यां ये विप्रा नो उपासते । कामं तान् धार्मिको राजा शूद्रकर्मसु योजयेद् ॥ इति ।
2.4.e: Now they quote with reference to this (subject) also the following two verses, which have been proclaimed by the Lord of created beings (Pra g āpati) 'How can those twice-born men be called Brāhmaṇas who do not perform their twilight devotions, in the morning and in the evening at the proper time? At his pleasure a righteous king may appoint those Brāhmaṇas who neglect to daily perform the twilight devotions, both at morn and at eve, to do the work of Śūdras.'

2.4.s: tatra sāyamatikrame rātryupavāsaḥprātaratikrame 'harupavāsaḥ |
2.4.d: तत्र सायमतिक्रमे रात्र्युपवासःप्रातरतिक्रमे ऽहरुपवासः ।
2.4.e: If the time for the (twilight devotion) is allowed to pass in the evening, (the offender shall) fast during the night; and if it is neglected in the morning, he shall fast during the (next) day.

2.4.s: sthānāsanaphalam avāpnoti |
2.4.d: स्थानासनफलम् अवाप्नोति ।
2.4.e: He obtains (thereby) the (same) reward as if he had remained standing and sitting (in the twilight).

2.4.s: athāpy udāharanti | yad upasthakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ padbhyāṃ vā yat kṛtaṃ bhavet | bāhubhyāṃ manasā vāpi vācā vā yat kṛtaṃ bhavet | sāyaṃ saṃdhyām upasthāya tena tasmāt pramucyate |
2.4.d: अथाप्य् उदाहरन्ति । यद् उपस्थकृतं पापं पद्भ्यां वा यत् कृतं भवेत् । बाहुभ्यां मनसा वापि वाचा वा यत् कृतं भवेत् । सायं संध्याम् उपस्थाय तेन तस्मात् प्रमुच्यते ।
2.4.e: Now they quote also (the following verses): 'Whatever sin (a man) may have committed with his organ, with his feet, with his arms, by thoughts or by speech, from (all) that he is freed by performing the twilight devotion in the evening.'

2.4.s: rātryā cāpi saṃdhīyate na cainaṃ varuṇo gṛhṇāti |
2.4.d: रात्र्या चापि संधीयते न चैनं वरुणो गृह्णाति ।
2.4.e: (The worshipper) becomes also connected (thereby) with the (next) night, and Varuṇa will not seize him.

2.4.s: evam eva prātar upasthāya rātrikṛtāt pāpāt pramucyate |
2.4.d: एवम् एव प्रातर् उपस्थाय रात्रिकृतात् पापात् प्रमुच्यते ।
2.4.e: In like manner he becomes free from the sin committed during the night by worshipping in the morning.

2.4.s: ahnā cāpi saṃdhīyate mitraś cainaṃ gopāyaty ādityaścainaṃ svargaṃ lokam unnayati |
2.4.d: अह्ना चापि संधीयते मित्रश् चैनं गोपायत्य् आदित्यश्चैनं स्वर्गं लोकम् उन्नयति ।
2.4.e: He is also connected with the (next) day, Mitra protects him and Āditya leads him up to heaven.

2.4.s: sa evam evāharahar ahorātrayoḥ saṃdhiṣūpatiṣṭhamānobrahmapūto brahmabhūto brāhmaṇaḥ śāstram anuvartamāno brahmalokam abhijayatīti vijñāyate | brahmalokam abhijayatīti vijñāyate |
2.4.d: स एवम् एवाहरहर् अहोरात्रयोः संधिषूपतिष्ठमानोब्रह्मपूतो ब्रह्मभूतो ब्राह्मणः शास्त्रम् अनुवर्तमानो ब्रह्मलोकम् अभिजयतीति विज्ञायते । ब्रह्मलोकम् अभिजयतीति विज्ञायते ।
2.4.e: It is declared in the Veda, 'A Brāhmaṇa who in this same manner daily worships in the twilight, both at morn and at eve and, being sanctified by the Brahman, becoming one with the Brahman, and resplendent through the Brahman, follows the rules of the Śāstra, gains the heaven of Brahman.'

2.5.s: atha hastau prakṣālya kamaṇḍaluṃ mṛtpiṇḍaṃ ca saṃgṛhya tīrthaṃ gatvā triḥ pādau prakṣālayate trir ātmānaṃ |
2.5.d: अथ हस्तौ प्रक्षाल्य कमण्डलुं मृत्पिण्डं च संगृह्य तीर्थं गत्वा त्रिः पादौ प्रक्षालयते त्रिर् आत्मानं ।
2.5.e: Now, after washing his hands, he shall take his waterpot and a clod of earth, go to a (sacred) bathing-place and thrice clean his feet (with earth and water) and thrice his body.

2.5.s: atha haike bruvate | śmaśānam āpo devagṛhaṃ goṣṭhaṃ yatra cabrāhmaṇā aprakṣālya pādau tan na praveṣṭavyam iti |
2.5.d: अथ हैके ब्रुवते । श्मशानम् आपो देवगृहं गोष्ठं यत्र चब्राह्मणा अप्रक्षाल्य पादौ तन् न प्रवेष्टव्यम् इति ।
2.5.e: Now some say, 'One must not enter a burial-ground, water, a temple, a cowpen, nor a place where Brāhmaṇas (sit) without having cleaned one's feet.'

2.5.s: athāpo 'bhiprapadyate | hiraṇyaśṛṅgaṃ varuṇaṃ prapadye tīrthaṃ me dehi yācitaḥ | yan mayā bhuktam asādhūnāṃ pāpebhyaś ca pratigrahaḥ | yan me manasā vācā karmaṇā vā duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam | tan na indro varuṇo bṛhaspatiḥ savitā ca punantupunaḥpunaḥ || iti |
2.5.d: अथापो ऽभिप्रपद्यते । हिरण्यशृङ्गं वरुणं प्रपद्ये तीर्थं मे देहि याचितः । यन् मया भुक्तम् असाधूनां पापेभ्यश् च प्रतिग्रहः । यन् मे मनसा वाचा कर्मणा वा दुष्कृतं कृतम् । तन् न इन्द्रो वरुणो बृहस्पतिः सविता च पुनन्तुपुनःपुनः ॥ इति ।
2.5.e: Then he enters the water, (reciting the following verse): 'I take refuge with gold-horned Varuṇa, give me at my request (O Varuṇa) a purifying bathing-place. May Indra, Varuṇa, B ri haspati, and Savit ri again and again cleanse me from all sin which I have committed by eating the food of unholy men, by receiving gifts from the wicked, and from all evil which I have done by thoughts, speeches, or deeds.'

2.5.s: athāñjalināpa upahanti | sumitrā na āpa oṣadhayaḥ santv iti |
2.5.d: अथाञ्जलिनाप उपहन्ति । सुमित्रा न आप ओषधयः सन्त्व् इति ।
2.5.e: Then he takes up water in his joined hands, (saying), 'May the waters and the herbs be propitious to us.'

2.5.s: tāṃ diśaṃ nirukṣati yasyām asya diśi dveṣyo bhavati | durmitrās tasmai bhūyāsur yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣma iti |
2.5.d: तां दिशं निरुक्षति यस्याम् अस्य दिशि द्वेष्यो भवति । दुर्मित्रास् तस्मै भूयासुर् यो ऽस्मान् द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्म इति ।
2.5.e: (Next) he pours (the water) out in that direction in which an enemy of his dwells, (saying), 'May they work woe to him who hates us and whom we hate.'

2.5.s: athāpa upaspṛśya triḥ pradakṣiṇam udakam āvartayati | yadapāṃ kruraṃ yad amedhyaṃ yad aśāntaṃ tad apagacchatād iti |
2.5.d: अथाप उपस्पृश्य त्रिः प्रदक्षिणम् उदकम् आवर्तयति । यदपां क्रुरं यद् अमेध्यं यद् अशान्तं तद् अपगच्छताद् इति ।
2.5.e: Then he sips water, and thrice makes the water eddy around himself turning from the left to the right (and saying), 'May that which is hurtful, which is impure, and which is inauspicious in the water be removed.'

2.5.s: apsu nimajjyonmajjya |
2.5.d: अप्सु निमज्ज्योन्मज्ज्य ।
2.5.e: After having submerged himself and having emerged from the water,

2.5.s: nāpsu sataḥ prayamaṇaṃ vidyate na vāsaḥpalpūlanaṃnopasparśanam |
2.5.d: नाप्सु सतः प्रयमणं विद्यते न वासःपल्पूलनंनोपस्पर्शनम् ।
2.5.e: (Acts of) personal purification, washing the clothes by beating them on a stone and sipping water are not (permitted to the worshipper) as long as he is in the water.

2.5.s: yady uparuddhāḥ syur etenopatiṣṭhate | namo 'gnaye 'psumatenama indrāya namo varuṇāya namo vāruṇyai namo 'dbhya iti |
2.5.d: यद्य् उपरुद्धाः स्युर् एतेनोपतिष्ठते । नमो ऽग्नये ऽप्सुमतेनम इन्द्राय नमो वरुणाय नमो वारुण्यै नमो ऽद्भ्य इति ।
2.5.e: If (the water used for bathing) has been (taken from a) confined (place, such as a well), he worships it with the following (Mantra): 'Adoration to Agni, the lord of the waters; adoration to Indra; adoration to Varuṇa; adoration to Vāruṇī; adoration to the waters.'

2.5.s: uttīryācamyācāntaḥ punar ācāmet | āpaḥ punantu pṛthivīṃ pṛthivī pūtā punātu mām | punantu brahmaṇaspatir brahma pūtā punātu mām | yad ucchiṣṭam abhojyaṃ yad vā duścaritaṃ mama | sarvaṃ punantu mām āpo 'satāṃ ca pratigrahaṃ svāheti |
2.5.d: उत्तीर्याचम्याचान्तः पुनर् आचामेत् । आपः पुनन्तु पृथिवीं पृथिवी पूता पुनातु माम् । पुनन्तु ब्रह्मणस्पतिर् ब्रह्म पूता पुनातु माम् । यद् उच्छिष्टम् अभोज्यं यद् वा दुश्चरितं मम । सर्वं पुनन्तु माम् आपो ऽसतां च प्रतिग्रहं स्वाहेति ।
2.5.e: After having ascended the bank and having sipped water, let him again sip water, though he has done so before, (and recite the following Mantras) 'May water purify the earth, may the purified earth purify me, may Brahmaṇaspati (and) Brahman purify, may the purified (earth) purify me. May water purify me, (taking away) all (the guilt which I incurred by eating) remnants of food, and forbidden food, (by committing) evil deeds, (by) receiving gifts from wicked men, Svāhā!'

2.5.s: pavitre kṛtvādbhir mārjayati | āpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuva ititisṛbhiḥ | hiraṇyavarṇāḥ śucayaḥ pāvakā iti catasṛbhiḥ | pavamānaḥsuvarjana iti | etenānuvākena mārjayitvāntarjalagato 'ghamarṣaṇena trīn prāṇāyāmān dhārayitvottīrya vāsaḥ pīḍayitvā prakṣālitopavātānyakliṣṭāni vāsāṃsi paridhāyāpa ācamya darbheṣv āsīno darbhāndhārayamāṇaḥ prāṅmukhaḥ sāvitrīṃ sahasrakṛtva āvartayec chatakṛtvo 'parimitakṛtvo vā daśāvaram |
2.5.d: पवित्रे कृत्वाद्भिर् मार्जयति । आपो हि ष्ठा मयोभुव इतितिसृभिः । हिरण्यवर्णाः शुचयः पावका इति चतसृभिः । पवमानःसुवर्जन इति । एतेनानुवाकेन मार्जयित्वान्तर्जलगतो ऽघमर्षणेन त्रीन् प्राणायामान् धारयित्वोत्तीर्य वासः पीडयित्वा प्रक्षालितोपवातान्यक्लिष्टानि वासांसि परिधायाप आचम्य दर्भेष्व् आसीनो दर्भान्धारयमाणः प्राङ्मुखः सावित्रीं सहस्रकृत्व आवर्तयेच् छतकृत्वो ऽपरिमितकृत्वो वा दशावरम् ।
2.5.e: Making two Pavitras he rubs (his body) with water. Having rubbed himself, (reciting the) three (verses), 'Ye waters are,' &c., the four (verses), 'The golden-coloured, pure, purifying,' &c., (and) the Anuvāka, 'He who purifies,' &c., he performs, stepping back into the water, three Prāṇāyāmas with the Aghamarshaṇa (hymn); then he ascends the bank, squeezes (the water) out of his dress, puts on garments which have been washed and dried in the air and which are not the worse for wear, sips water, sits down on Darbha grass, and, holding Darbha grass (in his hands), recites, facing the east, the Gāyatrī one thousand times, (or) one hundred times, or any number of times, or at least twelve times.

2.5.s: athādityam upatiṣṭhate | ud vayaṃ tamasas pari | ud u tyam | citram | tac cakṣur devahitam | ya udagād iti |
2.5.d: अथादित्यम् उपतिष्ठते । उद् वयं तमसस् परि । उद् उ त्यम् । चित्रम् । तच् चक्षुर् देवहितम् । य उदगाद् इति ।
2.5.e: Then he worships the sun (reciting the following Mantras): 'Out of darkness we,' &c., 'Up that bright,' &c., That eye which is beneficial to the gods,' &c., (and) 'He who rose,' &c.

2.5.s: athāpy udāharanti | praṇavo vyāhṛtayaḥ sāvitrī cety etepañca brahmayajñā aharahar brāhmaṇaṃ kilbiṣāt pāvayanti |
2.5.d: अथाप्य् उदाहरन्ति । प्रणवो व्याहृतयः सावित्री चेत्य् एतेपञ्च ब्रह्मयज्ञा अहरहर् ब्राह्मणं किल्बिषात् पावयन्ति ।
2.5.e: Now they quote also (the following maxim): 'The syllable Om,, the Vyāh ri tis, and the Sāvitrī, these five Veda-offerings daily cleanse the Brāhmaṇa from guilt.'

2.5.s: pūtaḥ pañcabhir brahmayajñair athottaraṃ devatās tarpayati |
2.5.d: पूतः पञ्चभिर् ब्रह्मयज्ञैर् अथोत्तरं देवतास् तर्पयति ।
2.5.e: Being purified by the five Veda-offerings, he next satiates the gods (with water, saying),

2.5.s: om agniḥ prajāpatiḥ somo rudro 'ditir bṛhaspatiḥsarpā ity etāni prāgdvārāṇi daivatāni sanakṣatrāṇi sagrahāṇisāhorātrāṇi samuhūrtāni tarpayāmi | oṃ vasūṃś ca tarpayāmi |
2.5.d: ओम् अग्निः प्रजापतिः सोमो रुद्रो ऽदितिर् बृहस्पतिःसर्पा इत्य् एतानि प्राग्द्वाराणि दैवतानि सनक्षत्राणि सग्रहाणिसाहोरात्राणि समुहूर्तानि तर्पयामि । ओं वसूंश् च तर्पयामि ।
2.5.e: 'I satiate the deities of the eastern gate, Agni, Pra g āpati, Soma, Rudra, Aditi, B ri haspati, together with the lunar mansions, with the planets, with the days and nights, and with the Muhūrtas; Om, I also satiate the Vasus;

2.5.s: oṃ pitaro 'ryamā bhagaḥ savitā tvaṣṭā vāyurindrāgnī ity etāni dakṣiṇadvārāṇi daivatāni sanakṣatrāṇisagrahāṇi sāhorātrāṇi samuhūrtāni tarpayāmi | oṃ rudrāṃś ca tarpayāmi |
2.5.d: ओं पितरो ऽर्यमा भगः सविता त्वष्टा वायुरिन्द्राग्नी इत्य् एतानि दक्षिणद्वाराणि दैवतानि सनक्षत्राणिसग्रहाणि साहोरात्राणि समुहूर्तानि तर्पयामि । ओं रुद्रांश् च तर्पयामि ।
2.5.e: 'Om, I satiate the deities of the southern gate, the Pit ri s, Yama, Bhaga, Savit ri , Tvashṭri , Vāyu, Indrāgnī, together with the lunar mansions, with the planets, with the days and nights, and with the Muhūrtas; Om, I also satiate the Rudras.

2.5.s: oṃ mitra indro mahāpitara āpo viśve devā brahmāviṣṇur ity etāni pratyagdvārāṇi daivatāni sanakṣatrāṇi sagrahāṇisāhorātrāṇi samuhūrtāni tarpayāmi | om ādityāṃś ca tarpayāmi |
2.5.d: ओं मित्र इन्द्रो महापितर आपो विश्वे देवा ब्रह्माविष्णुर् इत्य् एतानि प्रत्यग्द्वाराणि दैवतानि सनक्षत्राणि सग्रहाणिसाहोरात्राणि समुहूर्तानि तर्पयामि । ओम् आदित्यांश् च तर्पयामि ।
2.5.e: 'Om, I satiate the deities of the western gate, Mitra, Indra, the Mahāpit ri s, the Waters, all the gods, Brahman, Vishṇu, together with the lunar mansions, with the planets, with the days and nights, and with the Muhūrtas; Om, I also satiate the Ādityas.

2.5.s: oṃ vasavo varuṇo 'ja ekapād ahirbudhnyaḥpūṣāśvinau yama ity etāny udagdvārāṇi daivatāni sanakṣatrāṇisagrahāṇi sāhorātrāṇi samuhūrtāni tarpayāmi | oṃ viśvāndevāṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ sādhyāṃś ca tarpayāmi |
2.5.d: ओं वसवो वरुणो ऽज एकपाद् अहिर्बुध्न्यःपूषाश्विनौ यम इत्य् एतान्य् उदग्द्वाराणि दैवतानि सनक्षत्राणिसग्रहाणि साहोरात्राणि समुहूर्तानि तर्पयामि । ओं विश्वान्देवांस् तर्पयामि । ओं साध्यांश् च तर्पयामि ।
2.5.e: 'Om, I satiate the deities of the northern gate, the Vasus, Varuṇa, A g a-ekapād, Ahibudhnya, Ushas, the two Aśvins, Yama, together with . . . . . .

2.5.s: oṃ brahmāṇaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ prajāpatiṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ caturmukhaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ parameṣṭhinaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ hiraṇyagarbhaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ svayaṃbhuvaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ brahmapārṣadāṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ brahmapārṣadīś ca tarpayāmi | om agniṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ vāyuṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ varuṇaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ sūryaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ candramasaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ nakṣatrāṇi tarpayāmi | oṃ sadyojātaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ bhūḥ puruṣaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ bhuvaḥ puruṣaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ suvaḥ puruṣaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ puruṣaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ bhūs tarpayāmi | oṃ bhuvas tarpayāmi | oṃ suvas tarpayāmi | oṃ mahas tarpayāmi | oṃ janas tarpayāmi | oṃ tapas tarpayāmi | oṃ satyaṃ tarpayāmi |
2.5.d: ओं ब्रह्माणं तर्पयामि । ओं प्रजापतिं तर्पयामि । ओं चतुर्मुखं तर्पयामि । ओं परमेष्ठिनं तर्पयामि । ओं हिरण्यगर्भं तर्पयामि । ओं स्वयंभुवं तर्पयामि । ओं ब्रह्मपार्षदांस् तर्पयामि । ओं ब्रह्मपार्षदीश् च तर्पयामि । ओम् अग्निं तर्पयामि । ओं वायुं तर्पयामि । ओं वरुणं तर्पयामि । ओं सूर्यं तर्पयामि । ओं चन्द्रमसं तर्पयामि । ओं नक्षत्राणि तर्पयामि । ओं सद्योजातं तर्पयामि । ओं भूः पुरुषं तर्पयामि । ओं भुवः पुरुषं तर्पयामि । ओं सुवः पुरुषं तर्पयामि । ओं भूर् भुवः सुवः पुरुषं तर्पयामि । ओं भूस् तर्पयामि । ओं भुवस् तर्पयामि । ओं सुवस् तर्पयामि । ओं महस् तर्पयामि । ओं जनस् तर्पयामि । ओं तपस् तर्पयामि । ओं सत्यं तर्पयामि ।

2.5.s: oṃ bhavaṃ devaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ śarvaṃ devam tarpayāmi | omīśānaṃ devaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ paśupatiṃ devaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ rudraṃdevaṃ tarpayāmi | om ugraṃ devaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ bhīmaṃ devaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ mahāntaṃ devaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ bhavasya devasya patnīṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ śarvasya devasyapatnīṃ tarpayāmi | om īśānasya devasya patnīṃ tarpayāmi | oṃpaśupater devasya patnīṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ rudrasya devasya patnīṃ tarpayāmi | om ugrasya devasya patnīṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ bhīmasya devasyapatnīṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ mahato devasya patnīṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ bhavasya devasya sutaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ śarvasya devasyasutaṃ tarpayāmi | om īśānasya devasya sutaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ paśupaterdevasya sutaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ rudrasya devasya sutaṃ tarpayāmi | omugrasya devasya sutaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ bhīmasya devasya sutaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ mahato devasya sutaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ rudrāṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ rudrapārṣadāṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ rudrapārṣadīśca tarpayāmi |
2.5.d: ओं भवं देवं तर्पयामि । ओं शर्वं देवम् तर्पयामि । ओमीशानं देवं तर्पयामि । ओं पशुपतिं देवं तर्पयामि । ओं रुद्रंदेवं तर्पयामि । ओम् उग्रं देवं तर्पयामि । ओं भीमं देवं तर्पयामि । ओं महान्तं देवं तर्पयामि । ओं भवस्य देवस्य पत्नीं तर्पयामि । ओं शर्वस्य देवस्यपत्नीं तर्पयामि । ओम् ईशानस्य देवस्य पत्नीं तर्पयामि । ओंपशुपतेर् देवस्य पत्नीं तर्पयामि । ओं रुद्रस्य देवस्य पत्नीं तर्पयामि । ओम् उग्रस्य देवस्य पत्नीं तर्पयामि । ओं भीमस्य देवस्यपत्नीं तर्पयामि । ओं महतो देवस्य पत्नीं तर्पयामि । ओं भवस्य देवस्य सुतं तर्पयामि । ओं शर्वस्य देवस्यसुतं तर्पयामि । ओम् ईशानस्य देवस्य सुतं तर्पयामि । ओं पशुपतेर्देवस्य सुतं तर्पयामि । ओं रुद्रस्य देवस्य सुतं तर्पयामि । ओमुग्रस्य देवस्य सुतं तर्पयामि । ओं भीमस्य देवस्य सुतं तर्पयामि । ओं महतो देवस्य सुतं तर्पयामि । ओं रुद्रांस् तर्पयामि । ओं रुद्रपार्षदांस् तर्पयामि । ओं रुद्रपार्षदीश्च तर्पयामि ।

2.5.s: oṃ vighnaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ vināyakaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ vīraṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ sthūlaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ varadaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ hastimukhaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ vakratuṇḍaṃ tarpayāmi | om ekadantaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ lambodaraṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ vighnapārṣadāṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ vighnapārṣadīś ca tarpayāmi |
2.5.d: ओं विघ्नं तर्पयामि । ओं विनायकं तर्पयामि । ओं वीरं तर्पयामि । ओं स्थूलं तर्पयामि । ओं वरदं तर्पयामि । ओं हस्तिमुखं तर्पयामि । ओं वक्रतुण्डं तर्पयामि । ओम् एकदन्तं तर्पयामि । ओं लम्बोदरं तर्पयामि । ओं विघ्नपार्षदांस् तर्पयामि । ओं विघ्नपार्षदीश् च तर्पयामि ।

2.5.s: oṃ sanatkumāraṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ skandaṃ tarpayāmi | om indraṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ ṣaṣṭhīṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ ṣaṇmukhaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ jayantaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ viśākhaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ mahāsenaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃsubrahmaṇyaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ skandapārṣadāṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ skandapārṣadīś ca tarpayāmi |
2.5.d: ओं सनत्कुमारं तर्पयामि । ओं स्कन्दं तर्पयामि । ओम् इन्द्रं तर्पयामि । ओं षष्ठीं तर्पयामि । ओं षण्मुखं तर्पयामि । ओं जयन्तं तर्पयामि । ओं विशाखं तर्पयामि । ओं महासेनं तर्पयामि । ओंसुब्रह्मण्यं तर्पयामि । ओं स्कन्दपार्षदांस् तर्पयामि । ओं स्कन्दपार्षदीश् च तर्पयामि ।

2.5.s: om ādityaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ somaṃ tarpayāmi | om aṅgārakaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ budhaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ bṛhaspatiṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ śukraṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ śanaiścaraṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ rāhuṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ ketuṃ tarpayāmi |
2.5.d: ओम् आदित्यं तर्पयामि । ओं सोमं तर्पयामि । ओम् अङ्गारकं तर्पयामि । ओं बुधं तर्पयामि । ओं बृहस्पतिं तर्पयामि । ओं शुक्रं तर्पयामि । ओं शनैश्चरं तर्पयामि । ओं राहुं तर्पयामि । ओं केतुं तर्पयामि ।

2.5.s: oṃ keśavaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ nārāyaṇaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ mādhavaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ govindaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ viṣṇuṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ madhusūdanaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ trivikramaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ vāmanaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ śrīdharaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ hṛṣīkeśaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ padmanābhaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ dāmodaraṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ śriyaṃ devīṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ sarasvatīṃ devīṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ puṣṭiṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ tuṣṭiṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ garutmantaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ viṣṇupārṣadāṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ viṣṇupārṣadīś ca tarpayāmi |
2.5.d: ओं केशवं तर्पयामि । ओं नारायणं तर्पयामि । ओं माधवं तर्पयामि । ओं गोविन्दं तर्पयामि । ओं विष्णुं तर्पयामि । ओं मधुसूदनं तर्पयामि । ओं त्रिविक्रमं तर्पयामि । ओं वामनं तर्पयामि । ओं श्रीधरं तर्पयामि । ओं हृषीकेशं तर्पयामि । ओं पद्मनाभं तर्पयामि । ओं दामोदरं तर्पयामि । ओं श्रियं देवीं तर्पयामि । ओं सरस्वतीं देवीं तर्पयामि । ओं पुष्टिं तर्पयामि । ओं तुष्टिं तर्पयामि । ओं गरुत्मन्तं तर्पयामि । ओं विष्णुपार्षदांस् तर्पयामि । ओं विष्णुपार्षदीश् च तर्पयामि ।

2.5.s: oṃ yamaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ yamarājaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ dharmaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ dharmarājaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ kālaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ nīlaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ mṛtyuṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ vaivasvataṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ citraṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ citraguptaṃ tarpayāmi | om audumbaraṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ vaivasvatapārṣadāṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ vaivasvatapārṣadīśca tarpayāmi |
2.5.d: ओं यमं तर्पयामि । ओं यमराजं तर्पयामि । ओं धर्मं तर्पयामि । ओं धर्मराजं तर्पयामि । ओं कालं तर्पयामि । ओं नीलं तर्पयामि । ओं मृत्युं तर्पयामि । ओं वैवस्वतं तर्पयामि । ओं चित्रं तर्पयामि । ओं चित्रगुप्तं तर्पयामि । ओम् औदुम्बरं तर्पयामि । ओं वैवस्वतपार्षदांस् तर्पयामि । ओं वैवस्वतपार्षदीश्च तर्पयामि ।

2.5.s: oṃ bhūmidevāṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ kāśyapam tarpayāmi | om antarikṣaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ vidyāṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ dhanvantariṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ dhanvantaripārṣadāṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ dhanvantaripārṣadīś ca tarpayāmīti |
2.5.d: ओं भूमिदेवांस् तर्पयामि । ओं काश्यपम् तर्पयामि । ओम् अन्तरिक्षं तर्पयामि । ओं विद्यां तर्पयामि । ओं धन्वन्तरिं तर्पयामि । ओं धन्वन्तरिपार्षदांस् तर्पयामि । ओं धन्वन्तरिपार्षदीश् च तर्पयामीति ।

2.5.s: atha nivītī |
2.5.d: अथ निवीती ।
2.5.e: Next, passing the sacrificial thread round the neck, (he offers the following libations):

2.5.s: om ṛṣīṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ maharṣīṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ paramarṣīṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ brahmarṣīṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ devarṣīṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ rājarṣīṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ śrutarṣīṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ janarṛṣīṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ taparṛṣīṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ satyarṣīṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ saptarṣīṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ kāṇḍarṣīṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ ṛṣikāṃs tarpayāmi | om ṛṣipatnīs tarpayāmi | om ṛṣiputrāṃs tarpayāmi | om ṛṣipautrāṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ kāṇvaṃ baudhāyanaṃ tarpayāmi | om āpastambaṃ sūtrakāraṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ satyāṣāḍhaṃhiraṇyakeśinaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ vājasaneyinaṃ yājñavalkyam tarpayāmi | om āśvalāyanaṃ śaunakaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ vyāsaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ praṇavaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ vyāhṛtīs tarpayāmi | oṃ sāvitrīṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ gāyatrīṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ chandāṃsi tarpayāmi | om ṛgvedaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ yajurvedaṃ tarpayāmi | oṃ sāmavedaṃ tarpayāmi | om atharvavedaṃ tarpayāmi | om atharvāṅgirasas tarpayāmi | om itihāsapurāṇāni tarpayāmi | oṃ sarvavedāṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ sarvadevajanāṃs tarpayāmi | oṃ sarvabhūtāni tarpayāmīti |
2.5.d: ओम् ऋषींस् तर्पयामि । ओं महर्षींस् तर्पयामि । ओं परमर्षींस् तर्पयामि । ओं ब्रह्मर्षींस् तर्पयामि । ओं देवर्षींस् तर्पयामि । ओं राजर्षींस् तर्पयामि । ओं श्रुतर्षींस् तर्पयामि । ओं जनरृषींस् तर्पयामि । ओं तपरृषींस् तर्पयामि । ओं सत्यर्षींस् तर्पयामि । ओं सप्तर्षींस् तर्पयामि । ओं काण्डर्षींस् तर्पयामि । ओं ऋषिकांस् तर्पयामि । ओम् ऋषिपत्नीस् तर्पयामि । ओम् ऋषिपुत्रांस् तर्पयामि । ओम् ऋषिपौत्रांस् तर्पयामि । ओं काण्वं बौधायनं तर्पयामि । ओम् आपस्तम्बं सूत्रकारं तर्पयामि । ओं सत्याषाढंहिरण्यकेशिनं तर्पयामि । ओं वाजसनेयिनं याज्ञवल्क्यम् तर्पयामि । ओम् आश्वलायनं शौनकं तर्पयामि । ओं व्यासं तर्पयामि । ओं वसिष्ठं तर्पयामि । ओं प्रणवं तर्पयामि । ओं व्याहृतीस् तर्पयामि । ओं सावित्रीं तर्पयामि । ओं गायत्रीं तर्पयामि । ओं छन्दांसि तर्पयामि । ओम् ऋग्वेदं तर्पयामि । ओं यजुर्वेदं तर्पयामि । ओं सामवेदं तर्पयामि । ओम् अथर्ववेदं तर्पयामि । ओम् अथर्वाङ्गिरसस् तर्पयामि । ओम् इतिहासपुराणानि तर्पयामि । ओं सर्ववेदांस् तर्पयामि । ओं सर्वदेवजनांस् तर्पयामि । ओं सर्वभूतानि तर्पयामीति ।

2.5.s: atha prācīnāvīti | oṃ pitqn svadhā namas tarpayāmi | oṃ pitāmahān svadhā namas tarpayāmi | oṃ prapitāmahān svadhā namas tarpayāmi | oṃ mātqḥ svadhānamas tarpayāmi | oṃ pitāmahīḥ svadhā namas tarpayāmi | oṃ prapitāmahīḥ svadhā namas tarpayāmi | oṃ mātāmahān svadhā namas tarpayāmi | oṃ mātuḥ pitāmahānsvadhā namas tarpayāmi | oṃ mātuḥ prapitāmahān svadhānamas tarpayāmi | oṃ mātāmahīḥ svadhā namas tarpayāmi | oṃ mātuḥ pitāmahīḥ svadhā namas tarpayāmi | oṃ mātuḥ prapitāmahīḥ svadhā namas tarpayāmi |
2.5.d: अथ प्राचीनावीति । ओं पित्qन् स्वधा नमस् तर्पयामि । ओं पितामहान् स्वधा नमस् तर्पयामि । ओं प्रपितामहान् स्वधा नमस् तर्पयामि । ओं मात्qः स्वधानमस् तर्पयामि । ओं पितामहीः स्वधा नमस् तर्पयामि । ओं प्रपितामहीः स्वधा नमस् तर्पयामि । ओं मातामहान् स्वधा नमस् तर्पयामि । ओं मातुः पितामहान्स्वधा नमस् तर्पयामि । ओं मातुः प्रपितामहान् स्वधानमस् तर्पयामि । ओं मातामहीः स्वधा नमस् तर्पयामि । ओं मातुः पितामहीः स्वधा नमस् तर्पयामि । ओं मातुः प्रपितामहीः स्वधा नमस् तर्पयामि ।

2.5.s: om ācāryān svadhā namas tarpayāmi | om ācāryapatnīḥ svadhā namas tarpayāmi | oṃ gurūn svadhānamas tarpayāmi | oṃ gurupatnīḥ svadhā namas tarpayāmi | oṃ sakhīn svadhā namas tarpayāmi | oṃ sakhipatnīḥ svadhā namas tarpayāmi | oṃ jñātīn svadhānamas tarpayāmi | oṃ jñātipatnīḥ svadhā namas tarpayāmi | om amātyān svadhā namas tarpayāmi | om amātyapatnīḥ svadhā namas tarpayāmi | oṃ sarvān svadhā namas tarpayāmi | oṃ sarvāḥ svadhā namas tarpayāmīti |
2.5.d: ओम् आचार्यान् स्वधा नमस् तर्पयामि । ओम् आचार्यपत्नीः स्वधा नमस् तर्पयामि । ओं गुरून् स्वधानमस् तर्पयामि । ओं गुरुपत्नीः स्वधा नमस् तर्पयामि । ओं सखीन् स्वधा नमस् तर्पयामि । ओं सखिपत्नीः स्वधा नमस् तर्पयामि । ओं ज्ञातीन् स्वधानमस् तर्पयामि । ओं ज्ञातिपत्नीः स्वधा नमस् तर्पयामि । ओम् अमात्यान् स्वधा नमस् तर्पयामि । ओम् अमात्यपत्नीः स्वधा नमस् तर्पयामि । ओं सर्वान् स्वधा नमस् तर्पयामि । ओं सर्वाः स्वधा नमस् तर्पयामीति ।

2.5.s: anutīrtham apa utsiñcati |
2.5.d: अनुतीर्थम् अप उत्सिञ्चति ।
2.5.e: He pours the water out from the several Tīrthas (of the hand sacred to the several deities).

2.5.s: ūrjaṃ vahantīr amṛtaṃ ghṛtaṃ payaḥ kīlālaṃ parisrutam | svadhā stha tarpayata me pitqn | tṛpyata tṛpyata tṛpyateti |
2.5.d: ऊर्जं वहन्तीर् अमृतं घृतं पयः कीलालं परिस्रुतम् । स्वधा स्थ तर्पयत मे पित्qन् । तृप्यत तृप्यत तृप्यतेति ।
2.5.e: (He recites at the end of the rite the following [paragraph continues] Mantra): '(Ye waters), who bring food, ambrosia, clarified butter, milk, and barley-gruel, are food for the manes; satiate my ancestors! May you be satiated, may you be satiated!'

2.5.s: naikavastro nārdravāsā daivāni karmāṇy anusaṃcaret |
2.5.d: नैकवस्त्रो नार्द्रवासा दैवानि कर्माण्य् अनुसंचरेत् ।
2.5.e: Let him not perform ceremonies in honour of the gods while his clothes are wet, or while he is dressed in one garment only,.

2.5.s: pitṛsaṃyuktāni cety ekeṣām | pitṛsaṃyuktāni cety ekeṣām |
2.5.d: पितृसंयुक्तानि चेत्य् एकेषाम् । पितृसंयुक्तानि चेत्य् एकेषाम् ।
2.5.e: Nor those connected with the manes. That is the opinion) of some (teachers).

2.6.s: atheme pañca mahāyajñāḥ | tāny eva mahāsattrāṇi | devayajñaḥ pitṛyajño bhūtayajño manuṣyayajño brahmayajña iti |
2.6.d: अथेमे पञ्च महायज्ञाः । तान्य् एव महासत्त्राणि । देवयज्ञः पितृयज्ञो भूतयज्ञो मनुष्ययज्ञो ब्रह्मयज्ञ इति ।
2.6.e: Now these five great sacrifices, which are also called the great sacrificial sessions, are the sacrifice to be offered to the gods, the sacrifice to be offered to the manes, the sacrifice to be offered to all beings, the sacrifice to be offered to men, (and) the sacrifice to be offered to Brahman,

2.6.s: aharahaḥ svāhākuryād ā kāṣṭhāt | tathaitaṃdevayajñaṃ samāpnoti |
2.6.d: अहरहः स्वाहाकुर्याद् आ काष्ठात् । तथैतंदेवयज्ञं समाप्नोति ।
2.6.e: Let him daily offer (something to the gods with the exclamation) Svāhā, be it only a piece of fuel. Thereby he performs that sacrifice to the gods.

2.6.s: aharahaḥ svadhākuryād odapātrāt | tathaitaṃpitṛyajñaṃ samāpnoti |
2.6.d: अहरहः स्वधाकुर्याद् ओदपात्रात् । तथैतंपितृयज्ञं समाप्नोति ।
2.6.e: Let him daily offer (something to the manes with the exclamation) Svadhā, be it only a vessel filled with water. Thereby he performs that sacrifice to the manes.

2.6.s: aharahar namaḥkuryād ā puṣpebhyaḥ | tathaitambhūtayajñaṃ samāpnoti |
2.6.d: अहरहर् नमःकुर्याद् आ पुष्पेभ्यः । तथैतम्भूतयज्ञं समाप्नोति ।
2.6.e: Let him daily pay reverence to (all beings) endowed with life. Thereby he performs that sacrifice to the beings.

2.6.s: aharahar brāhmaṇebhyo 'nnaṃ dadyād ā mūlaphalaśākebhyaḥ | tathaitaṃ manuṣyayajñaṃ samāpnoti |
2.6.d: अहरहर् ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ऽन्नं दद्याद् आ मूलफलशाकेभ्यः । तथैतं मनुष्ययज्ञं समाप्नोति ।
2.6.e: Let him daily give food to Brāhmaṇas, be it only roots, fruit, or vegetables. Thereby he performs that sacrifice to men.

2.6.s: aharahaḥ svādhyāyaṃ kuryād ā praṇavāt | tathaitaṃbrahmayajñaṃ samāpnoti |
2.6.d: अहरहः स्वाध्यायं कुर्याद् आ प्रणवात् । तथैतंब्रह्मयज्ञं समाप्नोति ।
2.6.e: Let him daily recite the Veda privately, be it only the syllable Om or the Vyāh ri tis. Thereby he performs that sacrifice to be offered to Brahman.

2.6.s: svādhyāyo vai brahmayajñaḥ | tasya ha vā etasyabrahmayajñasya vāg eva juhūr mana upabhṛc cakṣur dhruvā medhā sruvaḥsatyam avabhṛthaḥ svargo loka udayanam | yāvantaṃ ha vā imāṃ vittasyapūrṇāṃ dadat svargaṃ lokaṃ jayati tāvantaṃ lokaṃ jayati bhūyāṃsaṃ cākṣayyaṃ cāpa punarmṛtyuṃ jayatiya evaṃ vidvān svādhyāyam adhīte | tasmāt svādhyāyo 'dhyetavya itihi brāhmaṇam |
2.6.d: स्वाध्यायो वै ब्रह्मयज्ञः । तस्य ह वा एतस्यब्रह्मयज्ञस्य वाग् एव जुहूर् मन उपभृच् चक्षुर् ध्रुवा मेधा स्रुवःसत्यम् अवभृथः स्वर्गो लोक उदयनम् । यावन्तं ह वा इमां वित्तस्यपूर्णां ददत् स्वर्गं लोकं जयति तावन्तं लोकं जयति भूयांसं चाक्षय्यं चाप पुनर्मृत्युं जयतिय एवं विद्वान् स्वाध्यायम् अधीते । तस्मात् स्वाध्यायो ऽध्येतव्य इतिहि ब्राह्मणम् ।
2.6.e: 'The private recitation of the Veda is, indeed, the sacrifice to Brahman. At that sacrifice to Brahman speech, forsooth, (takes the place of) the G uhū, the internal organ (that of) the Upabh ri t, the eye (that of) the Dhruvā, the understanding (that of) the Sruva, truth (that of) the final bath, heaven (is) the conclusion of the sacrifice. He who, knowing this, daily recites the Veda to himself, gains as much heavenly bliss as, and more than, he who gives away this whole earth that is filled with wealth, and imperishable (beatitude), and conquers death. Therefore the Veda should be recited in private. Thus speaks the Brāhmaṇa.'

2.6.s: athāpy udāharanti | svabhyaktaḥ suhitaḥ sukhe śayaneśayāno yaṃ yaṃ kratum adhīte tena tenāsyeṣṭaṃ bhavatīti |
2.6.d: अथाप्य् उदाहरन्ति । स्वभ्यक्तः सुहितः सुखे शयनेशयानो यं यं क्रतुम् अधीते तेन तेनास्येष्टं भवतीति ।
2.6.e: Now they quote also (the following passage): 'If, well anointed, well fed, and lying on a comfortable couch, one recites (the portion of the Veda referring to) any sacrifice, one has offered it thereby.'

2.6.s: tasya ha vā etasya dharmasya caturdhā bhedam eka āhuḥ | adṛṣṭatvāt | ye catvāra iti | karmavādaḥ |
2.6.d: तस्य ह वा एतस्य धर्मस्य चतुर्धा भेदम् एक आहुः । अदृष्टत्वात् । ये चत्वार इति । कर्मवादः ।
2.6.e: Some (teachers) declare (that there is a text) which teaches a fourfold division of these sacred duties. (But) as no (other meaning is) perceptible, (the text) 'Four paths,' &c., refers to sacrificial rites.

2.6.s: aiṣṭikapāśukasaumikadārvihomāṇām |
2.6.d: ऐष्टिकपाशुकसौमिकदार्विहोमाणाम् ।
2.6.e: (Viz.) to Ishṭis, animal sacrifices, Soma sacrifices, and Darvīhomas.

2.6.s: tad eṣābhivadati | ye catvāraḥ pathayo devayānā antarā dyāvāpṛthivī viyanti | teṣāṃ yo ajyānim ajītim āvahāt tasmai no devāḥ pari datteha sarve || iti |
2.6.d: तद् एषाभिवदति । ये चत्वारः पथयो देवयाना अन्तरा द्यावापृथिवी वियन्ति । तेषां यो अज्यानिम् अजीतिम् आवहात् तस्मै नो देवाः परि दत्तेह सर्वे ॥ इति ।
2.6.e: The following (Rik) declares that, 'Four paths, leading to the world of. the gods, go severally from the earth to heaven. All ye gods, place us on that among them which will gain us undecaying prosperity.'

2.6.s: brahmacārī gṛhastho vānaprasthaḥ parivrājaka iti |
2.6.d: ब्रह्मचारी गृहस्थो वानप्रस्थः परिव्राजक इति ।
2.6.e: The student, the householder, the hermit in the woods, the ascetic (constitute the four orders).

2.6.s: brahmacārī guruśuśrūṣy ā maraṇāt |
2.6.d: ब्रह्मचारी गुरुशुश्रूष्य् आ मरणात् ।
2.6.e: A student (shall) obey his teacher until death.

2.6.s: vānaprastho vaikhānasaśāstrasamudācāraḥ |
2.6.d: वानप्रस्थो वैखानसशास्त्रसमुदाचारः ।
2.6.e: A hermit is he who regulates his conduct entirely according to the Institutes proclaimed by Vikhanas.

2.6.s: vaikhānaso vane mūlaphalāśī tapaḥśīlaḥ savaneṣūdakamupaspṛśañ śrāmaṇakenāgnim ādhāyāgrāmyabhojīdevapitṛbhūtamanuṣyarṣipūjakaḥ sarvātithiḥ pratiṣiddhavarjaṃbaiṣkam apy upayuñjīta | na phālakṛṣṭam adhitiṣṭhed grāmaṃ ca na praviśet | jaṭilaś cīrājinavāsā nātisāṃvatsaraṃ bhuñjīta |
2.6.d: वैखानसो वने मूलफलाशी तपःशीलः सवनेषूदकमुपस्पृशञ् श्रामणकेनाग्निम् आधायाग्राम्यभोजीदेवपितृभूतमनुष्यर्षिपूजकः सर्वातिथिः प्रतिषिद्धवर्जंबैष्कम् अप्य् उपयुञ्जीत । न फालकृष्टम् अधितिष्ठेद् ग्रामं च न प्रविशेत् । जटिलश् चीराजिनवासा नातिसांवत्सरं भुञ्जीत ।
2.6.e: A Vaikhānasa (shall live) in the forest, subsisting on roots and fruit, practising austerities and bathing at morn, noon, and eve; he shall kindle a fire according to the Śrāmaṇaka (rule); he shall eat wild-growing (vegetables and grain) only; he shall worship gods, manes, Bhūtas, men, and Ri shis; he shall receive hospitably (men of) all (castes) except those (with whom intercourse is) forbidden; he may even use the flesh of animals killed by carnivorous beasts; he shall not step on ploughed (land); and he shall not enter a village; he shall wear his hair in braids, and dress in (garments made of) bark or skins; he shall not eat anything that has been hoarded for more than a year.

2.6.s: parivrājakaḥ parityajya bandhūn aparigrahaḥ pravrajed yathāvidhi |
2.6.d: परिव्राजकः परित्यज्य बन्धून् अपरिग्रहः प्रव्रजेद् यथाविधि ।
2.6.e: An ascetic shall leave his relatives and, not attended by any one nor procuring any property, depart (from his house performing the customary ceremony) according to the rule.

2.6.s: araṇyaṃ gatvā |
2.6.d: अरण्यं गत्वा ।
2.6.e: He shall go into the forest (and live there).

2.6.s: śikhāmuṇḍaḥ |
2.6.d: शिखामुण्डः ।
2.6.e: He shall shave his hair excepting the top-lock.

2.6.s: kaupīnācchādanaḥ |
2.6.d: कौपीनाच्छादनः ।
2.6.e: He shall wear a cloth to cover his nakedness.

2.6.s: varṣāsv ekasthaḥ |
2.6.d: वर्षास्व् एकस्थः ।
2.6.e: He shall reside in one place during the rainy season.

2.6.s: kāṣāyavāsāḥ |
2.6.d: काषायवासाः ।
2.6.e: He shall wear a dress dyed yellowish-red.

2.6.s: sannamusale vyaṅgāre nivṛttaśarāvasaṃpāte bhikṣeta |
2.6.d: सन्नमुसले व्यङ्गारे निवृत्तशरावसंपाते भिक्षेत ।
2.6.e: He shall go to beg when the pestle lies motionless, when the embers have been extinguished, and when the cleaning of the dishes has been finished.

2.6.s: vāṅmanaḥkarmadaṇḍair bhūtānām adrohī |
2.6.d: वाङ्मनःकर्मदण्डैर् भूतानाम् अद्रोही ।
2.6.e: With the three means of punishment, (viz.) words, thoughts, and acts, he shall not injure created beings.

2.6.s: pavitraṃ bibhrac chaucārtham |
2.6.d: पवित्रं बिभ्रच् छौचार्थम् ।
2.6.e: He shall carry a cloth for straining water for the sake of purification.

2.6.s: uddhṛtaparipūtābhir adbhir apkāryaṃ kurvāṇaḥ |
2.6.d: उद्धृतपरिपूताभिर् अद्भिर् अप्कार्यं कुर्वाणः ।
2.6.e: He shall perform the necessary purifications with water which has been taken out (of a well or tank) and has been strained.

2.6.s: apavidhya vaidikāni karmāṇy ubhayataḥ paricchinnā madhyamaṃpadaṃ saṃśliṣyāmaha iti vadantaḥ |
2.6.d: अपविध्य वैदिकानि कर्माण्य् उभयतः परिच्छिन्ना मध्यमंपदं संश्लिष्यामह इति वदन्तः ।
2.6.e: (Ascetics shall) say, 'Renouncing the works taught in the Veda, cut off from both (worlds), we attach ourselves to the central sphere (Brahman).'

2.6.s: aikāśramyaṃ tv ācāryā aprajanatvād itareṣām |
2.6.d: ऐकाश्रम्यं त्व् आचार्या अप्रजनत्वाद् इतरेषाम् ।
2.6.e: But the venerable teacher (declares) that there is one order only, because the others do not beget offspring.

2.6.s: tatrodāharanti | prāhlādir ha vai kapilo nāmāsura āsa | sa etān bhedāṃś cakāra devaiḥ spardhamānaḥ | tān manīṣī nādriyeta |
2.6.d: तत्रोदाहरन्ति । प्राह्लादिर् ह वै कपिलो नामासुर आस । स एतान् भेदांश् चकार देवैः स्पर्धमानः । तान् मनीषी नाद्रियेत ।
2.6.e: With reference to this matter they quote also (the following passage): 'There was, forsooth, an Āsura, Kapila by name, the son of Prahlāda. Striving with the gods, he made these divisions. A wise man should not take heed of them.'

2.6.s: adṛṣṭatvāt | ye catvāra iti | karmavādaaiṣṭikapāśukasaumikadārvihomāṇām |
2.6.d: अदृष्टत्वात् । ये चत्वार इति । कर्मवादऐष्टिकपाशुकसौमिकदार्विहोमाणाम् ।
2.6.e: Because no (other meaning is) perceptible, (the text) 'Four paths,' &c., refers to sacrificial rites, (viz.) to Ishṭis, animal sacrifices, Soma sacrifices, Darvīhomas.

2.6.s: tad eṣābhyanūcyate | eṣa nityo mahimā brāhmaṇasya na karmaṇā vardhate nokanīyān | tasyaivātmā padavit taṃ viditvā na karmaṇā lipyatepāpakena || iti |
2.6.d: तद् एषाभ्यनूच्यते । एष नित्यो महिमा ब्राह्मणस्य न कर्मणा वर्धते नोकनीयान् । तस्यैवात्मा पदवित् तं विदित्वा न कर्मणा लिप्यतेपापकेन ॥ इति ।
2.6.e: With respect to this (question the following verse also) is quoted: 'That eternal greatness of the Brāhmaṇa is neither increased by works, nor diminished. The soul knows the nature of that (greatness); knowing that, he is not stained by evil deeds.'

2.6.s: sa brūyāt | yena sūryas tapati tejaseddhaḥ pitā putreṇa pitṛmānyoniyonau | nāvedavin manute taṃ bṛhantaṃ sarvānubhūm ātmānaṃ saṃparāye || iti |
2.6.d: स ब्रूयात् । येन सूर्यस् तपति तेजसेद्धः पिता पुत्रेण पितृमान्योनियोनौ । नावेदविन् मनुते तं बृहन्तं सर्वानुभूम् आत्मानं संपराये ॥ इति ।
2.6.e: If he says that, (let him reflect on the following verse): 'He who knows not the Veda, does not at death think of that great, all-perceiving soul, through which the sun, resplendent with brilliancy, gives warmth, and the father has a father through the son at his birth from the womb.'

2.6.s: ime ye nārvāṅ na paraś caranti na brāhmaṇāso nasutekarāsaḥ | ta ete vācam abhipadya pāpayā sirīs tantraṃ tanvateaprajajñaye || iti |
2.6.d: इमे ये नार्वाङ् न परश् चरन्ति न ब्राह्मणासो नसुतेकरासः । त एते वाचम् अभिपद्य पापया सिरीस् तन्त्रं तन्वतेअप्रजज्ञये ॥ इति ।
2.6.e: (Moreover), 'Those who, being neither true Brāhmaṇas nor performers of Soma sacrifices, work not for that which is near, nor for that which is far, take hold of the word and with sinful (speech) ignorantly perform the rites.'

2.6.s: prajābhir agne amṛtatvam aśyām | jāyamāno vai brāhmaṇastribhir ṛṇavā jāyate brahmacaryeṇarṣibhyo yajñena devebhyaḥ prajayāpitṛbhya iti | evam ṛṇasaṃyogavādinyo 'saṃkhyeyā bhavanti |
2.6.d: प्रजाभिर् अग्ने अमृतत्वम् अश्याम् । जायमानो वै ब्राह्मणस्त्रिभिर् ऋणवा जायते ब्रह्मचर्येणर्षिभ्यो यज्ञेन देवेभ्यः प्रजयापितृभ्य इति । एवम् ऋणसंयोगवादिन्यो ऽसंख्येया भवन्ति ।
2.6.e: There are innumerable (passages in the Veda) which refer to the debts (to be paid by a Brāhmaṇa), such as, 'May I obtain, O Agni, immortality through offspring;' 'A Brāhmaṇa on being born, (owes) a son to his ancestors,' &c.

2.6.s: trayīṃ vidyāṃ brahmacaryaṃ prajātiṃ śraddhāṃ tapoyajñam anupradānam | ya etāni kurvate tair it saha smo rajo bhūtvā dhvaṃsate 'nyat praśaṃsan || iti | dhvaṃsate 'nyat praśaṃsann iti |
2.6.d: त्रयीं विद्यां ब्रह्मचर्यं प्रजातिं श्रद्धां तपोयज्ञम् अनुप्रदानम् । य एतानि कुर्वते तैर् इत् सह स्मो रजो भूत्वा ध्वंसते ऽन्यत् प्रशंसन् ॥ इति । ध्वंसते ऽन्यत् प्रशंसन्न् इति ।
2.6.e: 'Those dwell with us, who fulfil the following (duties), the study of the three Vedas, the studentship, the procreation of offspring, faith, austerity, sacrificing, and giving gifts; he who praises other (duties) becomes dust and perishes.'

2.7.s: atha śālīnayāyāvarāṇām ātmayājināṃ prāṇāhutīr vyākhyāsyāmaḥ |
2.7.d: अथ शालीनयायावराणाम् आत्मयाजिनां प्राणाहुतीर् व्याख्यास्यामः ।
2.7.e: Now we will explain the oblations (offered) to the vital air (prāṇa) by Śālīnas (householders) and Yāyāvaras (vagrants), who sacrifice to the soul.

2.7.s: sarvāvaśyakāvasāne saṃmṛṣṭopalipte deśe prāṅmukha upaviśya tad bhūtam āhriyamāṇam | bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar om iti | upasthāya vācaṃ yacchet |
2.7.d: सर्वावश्यकावसाने संमृष्टोपलिप्ते देशे प्राङ्मुख उपविश्य तद् भूतम् आह्रियमाणम् । भूर् भुवः सुवर् ओम् इति । उपस्थाय वाचं यच्छेत् ।
2.7.e: At the end of all the necessary (daily rites), let him sit down, facing the east, in a place that has been well cleaned and smeared with cowdung; next let him worship that prepared (food) which is being brought. (saying), 'Bhū h , Bhuva h , Sva h , Om,' (and then) remain silent.

2.7.s: nyastam annaṃ mahāvyāhṛtibhiḥ pradakṣiṇam udakaṃ pariṣicyasavyena pāṇināvimuñcan | amṛtopastaraṇam asīti | purastād apaḥ pītvā pañcānnena prāṇāhutīr juhoti | prāṇe niviṣṭo 'mṛtaṃ juhomi | śivo mā viśāpradāhāya | prāṇāya svāhā | apāneniviṣṭo 'mṛtaṃ juhomi | śivo mā viśāpradāhāya | apānāya svāhā | vyāne niviṣṭo 'mṛtaṃ juhomi | śivo mā viśāpradāhāya | vyānāyasvāhā | udāne niviṣṭo 'mṛtaṃ juhomi | śivo mā viśāpradāhāya | udānāya svāhā | samāne niviṣṭo 'mṛtaṃ juhomi | śivo mā viśāpradāhāya | samānāya svāheti |
2.7.d: न्यस्तम् अन्नं महाव्याहृतिभिः प्रदक्षिणम् उदकं परिषिच्यसव्येन पाणिनाविमुञ्चन् । अमृतोपस्तरणम् असीति । पुरस्ताद् अपः पीत्वा पञ्चान्नेन प्राणाहुतीर् जुहोति । प्राणे निविष्टो ऽमृतं जुहोमि । शिवो मा विशाप्रदाहाय । प्राणाय स्वाहा । अपानेनिविष्टो ऽमृतं जुहोमि । शिवो मा विशाप्रदाहाय । अपानाय स्वाहा । व्याने निविष्टो ऽमृतं जुहोमि । शिवो मा विशाप्रदाहाय । व्यानायस्वाहा । उदाने निविष्टो ऽमृतं जुहोमि । शिवो मा विशाप्रदाहाय । उदानाय स्वाहा । समाने निविष्टो ऽमृतं जुहोमि । शिवो मा विशाप्रदाहाय । समानाय स्वाहेति ।
2.7.e: (Next) he pours water round the food which has been placed (before him), turning his right hand towards it, and reciting the Mahāvyāh ri tis; (afterwards), continuing to hold (the dish) with his left hand, he first drinks water, (saying), 'Thou art a substratum for ambrosia,' and (finally) offers five oblations of food to the vital airs, (reciting the texts), 'Full of reverence, I offer ambrosia to Prāṇa; mayest thou propitiously enter me, not in order to burn me. To Prāṇa, Svāhā!' &c.

2.7.s: pañcānnena prāṇāhutīr hutvā tūṣṇīṃ bhūyo vratayetprajāpatiṃ manasā dhyāyan | nāntarā vācaṃ visṛjet |
2.7.d: पञ्चान्नेन प्राणाहुतीर् हुत्वा तूष्णीं भूयो व्रतयेत्प्रजापतिं मनसा ध्यायन् । नान्तरा वाचं विसृजेत् ।
2.7.e: After offering the five oblations of food to the vital airs, let him finish his meal silently. Meditating in his heart on the lord of created beings, let him not emit speech while (eating),

2.7.s: yady antarā vācaṃ visṛjet | bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar omiti | japitvā punar eva bhuñjīta |
2.7.d: यद्य् अन्तरा वाचं विसृजेत् । भूर् भुवः सुवर् ओमिति । जपित्वा पुनर् एव भुञ्जीत ।
2.7.e: If he emits speech, he shall mutter 'Bhū h , Bhuva h , Sva h , Om,' and afterwards continue to eat.

2.7.s: tvakkeśanakhakīṭākhupurīṣāṇi dṛṣṭvā taṃ deśaṃ piṇḍam uddhṛtyādbhir abhyukṣya bhasmāvakīrya punar adbhiḥ prokṣya vācāca praśastam upayuñjīta |
2.7.d: त्वक्केशनखकीटाखुपुरीषाणि दृष्ट्वा तं देशं पिण्डम् उद्धृत्याद्भिर् अभ्युक्ष्य भस्मावकीर्य पुनर् अद्भिः प्रोक्ष्य वाचाच प्रशस्तम् उपयुञ्जीत ।
2.7.e: Now they quote also (the following rule): 'If he sees (bits of) skin, hair, nail-(parings), insects, or the dung of rats (in his food), 'he shall take out a lump, sprinkle that spot with water, scatter ashes on it, again sprinkle it with water, and use (the remainder of the food), after it has been declared fit (for use).'

2.7.s: athāpy udāharanti | āsīnaḥ prāṅmukho 'śnīyād vāgyato 'nnam akutsayan | askandayaṃs tanmanāś ca bhuktvā cāgnim upaspṛśed || iti |
2.7.d: अथाप्य् उदाहरन्ति । आसीनः प्राङ्मुखो ऽश्नीयाद् वाग्यतो ऽन्नम् अकुत्सयन् । अस्कन्दयंस् तन्मनाश् च भुक्त्वा चाग्निम् उपस्पृशेद् ॥ इति ।
2.7.e: Now they quote also (the following verse): 'He shall eat, seated with his face towards the east, silent, not despising his food, not scattering (fragments on the ground), and solely attend (to his dinner); and, after he has eaten, he shall touch fire.'

2.7.s: sarvabhakṣyāpūpakandamūlaphalamāṃsāni dantair nāvadyet |
2.7.d: सर्वभक्ष्यापूपकन्दमूलफलमांसानि दन्तैर् नावद्येत् ।
2.7.e: He shall not cut off with his teeth (pieces from) eatables (that must be swallowed) entire, (such as) cakes, bulbs, roots, fruit, and flesh.

2.7.s: nātisuhitaḥ |
2.7.d: नातिसुहितः ।
2.7.e: (Let him) not (eat) to repletion.

2.7.s: amṛtāpidhānam asīti | upariṣṭād apaḥ pītvācāntohṛdayadeśam abhimṛśati | prāṇānāṃ granthir asi rudro mā viśāntakaḥ | tenānnenāpyāyasveti |
2.7.d: अमृतापिधानम् असीति । उपरिष्टाद् अपः पीत्वाचान्तोहृदयदेशम् अभिमृशति । प्राणानां ग्रन्थिर् असि रुद्रो मा विशान्तकः । तेनान्नेनाप्यायस्वेति ।
2.7.e: After (dinner) he shall drink water, (reciting the text), 'Thou art 'a covering for ambrosia,' and stroke (the region of) the heart, (saying), 'Thou art the bond that connects the vital airs; (thou art) [paragraph continues] Rudra and Death; enter me; mayest thou grow through this food.'

2.7.s: punar ācamya dakṣiṇe pādāṅguṣṭhe pāṇī nisrāvayati | aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo 'ṅguṣṭhaṃ ca samāśritaḥ | īśaḥ sarvasya jagataḥ prabhuḥ prīṇāti viśvabhuk || iti |
2.7.d: पुनर् आचम्य दक्षिणे पादाङ्गुष्ठे पाणी निस्रावयति । अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषो ऽङ्गुष्ठं च समाश्रितः । ईशः सर्वस्य जगतः प्रभुः प्रीणाति विश्वभुक् ॥ इति ।
2.7.e: After sipping water a second time, he allows (the drops from) the hand to flow on the big toe of his right foot (and recites the following text): 'May the male be pleased, he who is of the size of a thumb, who occupies (a space of the size of) a thumb, who is the lord of the whole world, masterful, and the enjoyer of the universe.'

2.7.s: hutānumantraṇam ūrdhvahastaḥ samācaret | śraddhāyāṃprāṇe niviśyāmṛtaṃ hutam | prāṇam annenāpyāyasva | śraddhāyāmapāne niviśyāmṛtaṃ hutam | prāṇam annenāpyāyasva | śraddhāyāṃvyāne niviśyāmṛtaṃ hutam | prāṇam annenāpyāyasva | śraddhāyāmudāne niviśyāmṛtaṃ hutam | prāṇam annenāpyāyasva | śraddhāyāṃsamāne niviśyāmṛtaṃ hutam | prāṇam annenāpyāyasveti | pañcabhiḥ |
2.7.d: हुतानुमन्त्रणम् ऊर्ध्वहस्तः समाचरेत् । श्रद्धायांप्राणे निविश्यामृतं हुतम् । प्राणम् अन्नेनाप्यायस्व । श्रद्धायामपाने निविश्यामृतं हुतम् । प्राणम् अन्नेनाप्यायस्व । श्रद्धायांव्याने निविश्यामृतं हुतम् । प्राणम् अन्नेनाप्यायस्व । श्रद्धायामुदाने निविश्यामृतं हुतम् । प्राणम् अन्नेनाप्यायस्व । श्रद्धायांसमाने निविश्यामृतं हुतम् । प्राणम् अन्नेनाप्यायस्वेति । पञ्चभिः ।
2.7.e: Let him perform the subsequent consecration (anumantraṇa) of the (food which has been) offered, with raised arms, (and let him recite) the five (texts beginning), 'With faith, worshipping Prāṇa, (I have) offered ambrosia; mayest thou increase Prāṇa through this food,'

2.7.s: brahmaṇi ma ātmāmṛtatvāyeti |
2.7.d: ब्रह्मणि म आत्मामृतत्वायेति ।

2.7.s: akṣareṇa cātmānaṃ yojayet |
2.7.d: अक्षरेण चात्मानं योजयेत् ।

2.7.s: sarvakratuyājinām ātmayājī viśiṣyate |
2.7.d: सर्वक्रतुयाजिनाम् आत्मयाजी विशिष्यते ।

2.7.s: athāpy udāharanti |
2.7.d: अथाप्य् उदाहरन्ति ।

2.7.s: yathā hi tūlam aiṣīkam agnau protaṃ pradīpyate | tadvat sarvāṇi pāpāni dahyante hy ātmayājinaḥ |
2.7.d: यथा हि तूलम् ऐषीकम् अग्नौ प्रोतं प्रदीप्यते । तद्वत् सर्वाणि पापानि दह्यन्ते ह्य् आत्मयाजिनः ।
2.7.e: Now they quote also (the following verse): 'As cotton and reeds, thrown into a fire, blaze up, even so all the guilt of him who sacrifices to the soul is consumed;'

2.7.s: kevalāgho bhavati kevalādī | mogham annaṃ vindateapracetā iti |
2.7.d: केवलाघो भवति केवलादी । मोघम् अन्नं विन्दतेअप्रचेता इति ।
2.7.e: (Moreover), 'He who eats merely (in order to satisfy his own hunger) reaps only guilt. In vain (the fool) takes food.'

2.7.s: sa evam evāharahaḥ sāyaṃ prātar juhuyāt |
2.7.d: स एवम् एवाहरहः सायं प्रातर् जुहुयात् ।

2.7.s: adbhir vā sāyam |
2.7.d: अद्भिर् वा सायम् ।

2.7.s: athāpy udāharanti | agre bhojayed atithīn antarvatnīr anantaram | bālavṛddhāṃs tathā dīnān vyādhitāṃś ca viśeṣataḥ | adattvā tu ya etebhyaḥ pūrvaṃ bhuṅkte yathāvidhi | bhujyamāno na jānāti na sa bhuṅkte sa bhujyate |
2.7.d: अथाप्य् उदाहरन्ति । अग्रे भोजयेद् अतिथीन् अन्तर्वत्नीर् अनन्तरम् । बालवृद्धांस् तथा दीनान् व्याधितांश् च विशेषतः । अदत्त्वा तु य एतेभ्यः पूर्वं भुङ्क्ते यथाविधि । भुज्यमानो न जानाति न स भुङ्क्ते स भुज्यते ।
2.7.e: Now they quote also (the following verses): Let him first feed his guests, next the pregnant women, then the infants and the aged, thereafter the distressed and particularly the diseased. But he who eats first, without having given (food) to those (persons) according to the rule, does not know that he is being eaten. He does not eat, (but) he is eaten.'

2.7.s: pitṛdaivatabhṛtyānāṃ mātāpitror guros tathā | vāgyato vighasam aśnīyād evaṃ dharmo vidhīyate || iti |
2.7.d: पितृदैवतभृत्यानां मातापित्रोर् गुरोस् तथा । वाग्यतो विघसम् अश्नीयाद् एवं धर्मो विधीयते ॥ इति ।
2.7.e: 'Let him eat silently what remains, (after he has given their portions) to the manes, the gods, the servants, his parents, and his Gurus; that is declared to be the rule of the sacred law.'

2.7.s: athāpy udāharanti | aṣṭau grāsā muner bhakṣyāḥ ṣoḍaśāraṇyavāsinaḥ | dvātriṃśat tu gṛhasthasya amitaṃ brahmacāriṇaḥ |
2.7.d: अथाप्य् उदाहरन्ति । अष्टौ ग्रासा मुनेर् भक्ष्याः षोडशारण्यवासिनः । द्वात्रिंशत् तु गृहस्थस्य अमितं ब्रह्मचारिणः ।
2.7.e: Nov they quote also (the following verses): Eight mouthfuls are the meal of an ascetic, sixteen that of a hermit in the woods, thirty-two that of a householder, and an unlimited (quantity) that of a student.'

2.7.s: āhitāgnir anaḍvāṃś ca brahmacārī ca te trayaḥ | aśnanta eva sidhyanti naiṣāṃ siddhir anaśnatām || iti |
2.7.d: आहिताग्निर् अनड्वांश् च ब्रह्मचारी च ते त्रयः । अश्नन्त एव सिध्यन्ति नैषां सिद्धिर् अनश्नताम् ॥ इति ।
2.7.e: 'An Agnihotrin, a draught-ox, and, a student, those three can do their work only if they eat (much); without eating (much) they cannot do it.'

2.7.s: gṛhastho brahmacārī vā yo 'naśnaṃs tu tapaś caret | prāṇāgnihotralopena avakīrṇī bhavet tu saḥ |
2.7.d: गृहस्थो ब्रह्मचारी वा यो ऽनश्नंस् तु तपश् चरेत् । प्राणाग्निहोत्रलोपेन अवकीर्णी भवेत् तु सः ।
2.7.e: 'A householder, or a student who practises austerity by fasting, becomes an Avakīrṇin through the omission of the sacrifice to the vital airs;'

2.7.s: anyatra prāyaścittāt | prāyaścitte tad eva vidhānam |
2.7.d: अन्यत्र प्रायश्चित्तात् । प्रायश्चित्ते तद् एव विधानम् ।
2.7.e: Except when he performs a penance. In the case of a penance that (fasting) is the rule.

2.7.s: athāpy udāharanti | antarā prātarāśaṃ ca sāyamāśaṃ tathaiva ca | sadopavāsī bhavati yo na bhuṅkte kadācana |
2.7.d: अथाप्य् उदाहरन्ति । अन्तरा प्रातराशं च सायमाशं तथैव च । सदोपवासी भवति यो न भुङ्क्ते कदाचन ।
2.7.e: Now they quote also (the following verses): 'He who never eats between the morning and the evening meals, (obtains the same reward as he who) constantly fasts.'

2.7.s: prāṇāgnihotramantrāṃs tu niruddhe bhojane japet | tretāgnihotramantrāṃs tu dravyālābhe yathā japet || iti |
2.7.d: प्राणाग्निहोत्रमन्त्रांस् तु निरुद्धे भोजने जपेत् । त्रेताग्निहोत्रमन्त्रांस् तु द्रव्यालाभे यथा जपेत् ॥ इति ।
2.7.e: 'As in case one obtains no materials (for the sacrifice), one must mutter the sacred texts to be recited at the Agnihotra, offered in the three fires, even so one should mutter the texts to be recited at the Prāṇāgnihotra, when one is prevented from dining.'

2.7.s: evam ācaran brahmabhūyāya kalpate | brahmabhūyāya kalpata iti |
2.7.d: एवम् आचरन् ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते । ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पत इति ।
2.7.e: 'He who acts thus, will become one with Brahman.' Thus spake Pra g āpati (the lord of created beings).

2.8.s: pitryam āyuṣyaṃ svargyaṃ yaśasyaṃ puṣṭikarma ca |
2.8.d: पित्र्यम् आयुष्यं स्वर्ग्यं यशस्यं पुष्टिकर्म च ।
2.8.e: The offering to the manes secures long life and heaven, is worthy of praise and a rite ensuring prosperity.

2.8.s: trimadhus triṇāciketas trisuparṇaḥ pañcāgniḥṣaḍaṅgavic chīrṣako jyeṣṭhasāmakaḥ snātaka iti paṅktipāvanāḥ |
2.8.d: त्रिमधुस् त्रिणाचिकेतस् त्रिसुपर्णः पञ्चाग्निःषडङ्गविच् छीर्षको ज्येष्ठसामकः स्नातक इति पङ्क्तिपावनाः ।
2.8.e: Persons who sanctify the company are, a Trimadhu, a Triṇā k iketa, a Trisuparṇa, one who keeps five fires, and one who knows the six Aṅgas, one who performs the vow called Śiras, one who knows the Gyesh th asāman, (and) a Snātaka;

2.8.s: tadabhāve rahasyavit |
2.8.d: तदभावे रहस्यवित् ।
2.8.e: On failure of these, one who knows the (texts called) Rahasya.

2.8.s: ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmānīti śrāddhasya mahimā | tasmādevaṃvidaṃ sapiṇḍam apy āśayet |
2.8.d: ऋचो यजूंषि सामानीति श्राद्धस्य महिमा । तस्मादेवंविदं सपिण्डम् अप्य् आशयेत् ।
2.8.e: The Ri k-verses, the Ya g us-formulas, and the Sāmans (give) lustre to a funeral offering. Therefore he may feed (on that occasion) even a Sapiṇd a relation who (knows) those (texts).

2.8.s: rākṣoghnāni ca sāmāni svadhāvanti yajūṃṣi ca | madhvṛco 'tha pavitrāṇi śrāvayed āśayañ śanaiḥ |
2.8.d: राक्षोघ्नानि च सामानि स्वधावन्ति यजूंषि च । मध्वृचो ऽथ पवित्राणि श्रावयेद् आशयञ् शनैः ।
2.8.e: Let him who feeds (Brāhmaṇas at a funeral sacrifice) cause them to hear successively the Rakshoghna Sāmans, the Ya g us-formulas (called) Svadhāvat, the Ri k-verses (called) Madhu, and the (texts called) Pavitras.

2.8.s: caraṇavato 'nūcānān yonigotramantrāsaṃbaddhāñ śucīn mantravatas tryavarān ayujaḥ pūrvedyuḥ prātar evavā nimantrya sadarbhopakḷpteṣv āsaneṣu prāṅmukhān upaveśayatyudaṅmukhān vā |
2.8.d: चरणवतो ऽनूचानान् योनिगोत्रमन्त्रासंबद्धाञ् शुचीन् मन्त्रवतस् त्र्यवरान् अयुजः पूर्वेद्युः प्रातर् एववा निमन्त्र्य सदर्भोपकॢप्तेष्व् आसनेषु प्राङ्मुखान् उपवेशयत्युदङ्मुखान् वा ।
2.8.e: Having invited on the day before (the Śrāddha), or just in the morning, virtuous, pure (men), such as Trimadhus, who know the Vedāṅgas and the sacred texts, who are not related by marriage, nor members of the same family, nor connected through the Veda, at least three, (but always) an odd number, the (sacrificer) makes them sit down on prepared seats, covered with Darbha grass, facing the east or the north.

2.8.s: athaināṃs tilamiśrā apaḥ pratigrāhya gandhair mālyaiścālaṃkṛtya | agnau kariṣyāmīti | anujñāto gnim upasamādhāya saṃparistīryāgnimukhāt kṛtvānnasyaiva tisra āhutīr juhoti | somāya pitṛpītāya svadhā namaḥ svāhā | yamāyāṅgirasvate pitṛmate svadhā namaḥ svāhā | agnayekavyavāhanāya sviṣṭakṛte svadhā namaḥ svāheti |
2.8.d: अथैनांस् तिलमिश्रा अपः प्रतिग्राह्य गन्धैर् माल्यैश्चालंकृत्य । अग्नौ करिष्यामीति । अनुज्ञातो ग्निम् उपसमाधाय संपरिस्तीर्याग्निमुखात् कृत्वान्नस्यैव तिस्र आहुतीर् जुहोति । सोमाय पितृपीताय स्वधा नमः स्वाहा । यमायाङ्गिरस्वते पितृमते स्वधा नमः स्वाहा । अग्नयेकव्यवाहनाय स्विष्टकृते स्वधा नमः स्वाहेति ।
2.8.e: Then he offers to them water mixed with sesamum seed, adorns them with scents and garlands (and says), 'I wish to offer oblations in the fire.' [paragraph continues] When he has received permission (to do so), he heaps fuel on the sacred fire, scatters Kuśa grass around it, performs (all the ceremonies) up to the end of the Agnimukha, and offers three burnt oblations of food only, (reciting the following texts): 'To Soma, accompanied by the manes, Svāhā!' 'To Yama, accompanied by the Aṅgiras and by the manes, Svāhā!' 'To Agni, who carries the offerings to the manes, who causes sacrifices to be well performed, Svāhā!'

2.8.s: taccheṣeṇānnam abhighāryānnasyaitā eva tisro juhuyāt |
2.8.d: तच्छेषेणान्नम् अभिघार्यान्नस्यैता एव तिस्रो जुहुयात् ।
2.8.e: He shall make these three oblations with food only which has been sprinkled with the remainder of the (clarified butter).

2.8.s: vayasāṃ piṇḍaṃ dadyāt |
2.8.d: वयसां पिण्डं दद्यात् ।
2.8.e: Let him give a cake of food to the birds.

2.8.s: vayasāṃ hi pitaraḥ pratimayā carantīti vijñāyate |
2.8.d: वयसां हि पितरः प्रतिमया चरन्तीति विज्ञायते ।
2.8.e: For it is declared in the Veda, 'The manes roam about in the shape of birds.'

2.8.s: athetarat sāṅguṣṭhena pāṇinābhimṛśati |
2.8.d: अथेतरत् साङ्गुष्ठेन पाणिनाभिमृशति ।
2.8.e: Next he touches the (other food) with his hand and with the thumb,

2.8.s: pṛthivīsamantasya te 'gnir upadraṣṭarcas te mahimā dattasyāpramādāya pṛthivī te pātraṃ dyaurapidhānaṃ brahmaṇas tvā mukhe juhomi brāhmaṇānāṃ tvā vidyāvatāṃprāṇāpānayor juhomy akṣitam asi mā pitqṇāṃ kṣeṣṭhā amutrāmuṣmiṃloka iti | antarikṣasamantasya te vāyur upaśrotā yajūṃṣi te mahimā dattasyāpramādāya pṛthivī te pātraṃdyaur apidhānaṃ brahmaṇas tvā mukhe juhomi brāhmaṇānāṃ tvāvidyāvatāṃ prāṇāpānayor juhomy akṣitam asi mā pitāmahānāṃ kṣeṣṭhā amutrāmuṣmiṃ loka iti | dyusamantasya ta ādityo 'nukhyātāsāmāni te mahimā dattasya apramādāya pṛthivī te pātraṃ dyaurapidhānaṃ brahmaṇas tvā mukhe juhomi brāhmaṇānāṃ tvā vidyāvatāṃprāṇāpānayor juhomy akṣitam asi mā prapitāmahānāṃ kṣeṣṭhāamutrāmuṣmiṃ loka iti |
2.8.d: पृथिवीसमन्तस्य ते ऽग्निर् उपद्रष्टर्चस् ते महिमा दत्तस्याप्रमादाय पृथिवी ते पात्रं द्यौरपिधानं ब्रह्मणस् त्वा मुखे जुहोमि ब्राह्मणानां त्वा विद्यावतांप्राणापानयोर् जुहोम्य् अक्षितम् असि मा पित्qणां क्षेष्ठा अमुत्रामुष्मिंलोक इति । अन्तरिक्षसमन्तस्य ते वायुर् उपश्रोता यजूंषि ते महिमा दत्तस्याप्रमादाय पृथिवी ते पात्रंद्यौर् अपिधानं ब्रह्मणस् त्वा मुखे जुहोमि ब्राह्मणानां त्वाविद्यावतां प्राणापानयोर् जुहोम्य् अक्षितम् असि मा पितामहानां क्षेष्ठा अमुत्रामुष्मिं लोक इति । द्युसमन्तस्य त आदित्यो ऽनुख्यातासामानि ते महिमा दत्तस्य अप्रमादाय पृथिवी ते पात्रं द्यौरपिधानं ब्रह्मणस् त्वा मुखे जुहोमि ब्राह्मणानां त्वा विद्यावतांप्राणापानयोर् जुहोम्य् अक्षितम् असि मा प्रपितामहानां क्षेष्ठाअमुत्रामुष्मिं लोक इति ।
2.8.e: (And recites the following texts): 'Fire sees thee, who art co-extensive with the earth, the Ri k-verses are thy greatness, lest the gift be in vain; the earth is the vessel for thee, the sky the cover; I offer thee in the mouth of Brahman, I offer thee in the Prāṇa and the Apāna of learned Brāhmaṇas; thou art imperishable, mayest thou never fail to (the manes of our) fathers yonder, in the other world.' 'Air hears thee, who art co-extensive with the middle sphere, the Ya g us-formulas are thy greatness, lest the gift be in vain; the earth is the vessel for thee, the sky the cover; . . . mayest thou never fail to the (manes of our) grandfathers yonder, in the other world.' 'The sun reveals thee, who art co-extensive with the sky, the Sāmans are thy greatness, lest the gift be in vain; . . . . mayest thou never fail to the (manes of our) great-grandfathers yonder, in the other world.'

2.8.s: atha vai bhavati |
2.8.d: अथ वै भवति ।
2.8.e: Now indeed (that) happens (also which the following verses teach):

2.8.s: agnau karaṇaśeṣeṇa tad annam abhighārayet | niraṅguṣṭhaṃ tu yad dattaṃ na tat prīṇāti vai pitqn |
2.8.d: अग्नौ करणशेषेण तद् अन्नम् अभिघारयेत् । निरङ्गुष्ठं तु यद् दत्तं न तत् प्रीणाति वै पित्qन् ।
2.8.e: 'Let him sprinkle that food with the remainder of the burnt oblations. But what is given without (touching it with) the thumb does not gladden the manes.'

2.8.s: ubhayoḥ śākhayor muktaṃ pitṛbhyo 'nnaṃ niveditam | tad antaram upāsante asurā duṣṭacetasaḥ |
2.8.d: उभयोः शाखयोर् मुक्तं पितृभ्यो ऽन्नं निवेदितम् । तद् अन्तरम् उपासन्ते असुरा दुष्टचेतसः ।
2.8.e: 'The malevolent Asuras seek an opportunity (to snatch away) that food intended for the manes, which is not supported with both hands.'

2.8.s: yātudhānāḥ piśācāś ca pratilumpanti tad haviḥ | tiladāne hy adāyāś ca tathā krodhavaśe 'surāḥ |
2.8.d: यातुधानाः पिशाचाश् च प्रतिलुम्पन्ति तद् हविः । तिलदाने ह्य् अदायाश् च तथा क्रोधवशे ऽसुराः ।
2.8.e: 'The Yātudhānas and Piśā k as, who receive no share, steal the food if sesamum grains are not scattered (on the seats of the guests), and the Asuras (take it) if (the host) is under the sway of anger.'

2.8.s: kāṣāyavāsā yān kurute japahomapratigrahān | na tad devaṃgamaṃ bhavati havyakavyeṣuyad haviḥ |
2.8.d: काषायवासा यान् कुरुते जपहोमप्रतिग्रहान् । न तद् देवंगमं भवति हव्यकव्येषुयद् हविः ।
2.8.e: 'If a person dressed in reddish clothes mutters prayers, offers burnt oblations, or receives gifts, the sacrificial viands, offered at sacrifices to the gods or to the manes, do not reach the deities.'

2.8.s: yac ca dattam anaṅguṣṭhaṃ yac caiva pratigṛhyate | ācāmati ca yas tiṣṭhan na sa tena samṛdhyate || iti |
2.8.d: यच् च दत्तम् अनङ्गुष्ठं यच् चैव प्रतिगृह्यते । आचामति च यस् तिष्ठन् न स तेन समृध्यते ॥ इति ।
2.8.e: 'If gifts are given or received without (touching them with) the thumb and, if one sips water standing, (the performer of the act) is not benefited thereby.'

2.8.s: ādyantayor apāṃ pradānaṃ sarvatra |
2.8.d: आद्यन्तयोर् अपां प्रदानं सर्वत्र ।
2.8.e: At the beginning and at the end (of a Śrāddha) water must be giver. (to the guests).

2.8.s: jayaprabhṛti yathāvidhānam |
2.8.d: जयप्रभृति यथाविधानम् ।
2.8.e: In every case the muttering (of sacred texts) and the other (necessary acts must be performed) according to the rule.

2.8.s: śeṣam uktam aṣṭakāhome |
2.8.d: शेषम् उक्तम् अष्टकाहोमे ।
2.8.e: The remaining (rules) have been prescribed (in the section) on the burnt oblations on Ashṭakā (days).

2.8.s: dvau daive pitṛkārye trīn ekaikam ubhayatra vā | bhojayet susamṛddho 'pi na prasajyeta vistare |
2.8.d: द्वौ दैवे पितृकार्ये त्रीन् एकैकम् उभयत्र वा । भोजयेत् सुसमृद्धो ऽपि न प्रसज्येत विस्तरे ।
2.8.e: 'He shall feed two (Brāhmaṇas) at the offering to the gods and three at the offering to the manes, or a single man on either occasion. Even a very wealthy man shall not be anxious (to entertain) a large company.'

2.8.s: satkriyāṃ deśakālau ca śaucaṃ brāhmaṇasaṃpadam | pañcaitān vistaro hanti tasmāt taṃ parivarjayet |
2.8.d: सत्क्रियां देशकालौ च शौचं ब्राह्मणसंपदम् । पञ्चैतान् विस्तरो हन्ति तस्मात् तं परिवर्जयेत् ।
2.8.e: 'A large company destroys these five (advantages), the respectful treatment (of the invited guests, the propriety of) time and place, purity and (the selection of) virtuous Brāhmaṇa (guests); therefore he shall not invite (a large number).'

2.8.s: urastaḥ pitaras tasya vāmataś ca pitāmahāḥ | dakṣiṇataḥ prapitāmahāḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ piṇḍatarkakāḥ || iti |
2.8.d: उरस्तः पितरस् तस्य वामतश् च पितामहाः । दक्षिणतः प्रपितामहाः पृष्ठतः पिण्डतर्ककाः ॥ इति ।
2.8.e: 'In front (feed) the fathers of the (sacrificer), to the left the grandfathers, to the right the great-grandfathers, and at the back those who pare off (portions) from the cakes.'

2.9.e: (Now follows some) advice for him who is desirous of offspring.
The two Aśvins have declared, that fame is gained by the procreation (of sons);

2.9.s: āyuṣā tapasā yuktaḥ svādhyāyejyāparāyaṇaḥ | prajām utpādayed yuktaḥ svesve varṇe jitendriyaḥ |
2.9.d: आयुषा तपसा युक्तः स्वाध्यायेज्यापरायणः । प्रजाम् उत्पादयेद् युक्तः स्वेस्वे वर्णे जितेन्द्रियः ।
2.9.e: 'Performing acts which tend to prolong life and austerities, intent on the performance of the private recitation and of sacrifices, and keeping his organs in subjection, let him carefully beget offspring in his own caste.'

2.9.s: brāhmaṇasyarṇasaṃyogas tribhir bhavati janmataḥ | tāni mucyātmavān bhavati vimukto dharmasaṃśayāt |
2.9.d: ब्राह्मणस्यर्णसंयोगस् त्रिभिर् भवति जन्मतः । तानि मुच्यात्मवान् भवति विमुक्तो धर्मसंशयात् ।
2.9.e: 'From his birth a Brāhmaṇa is loaded with three debts; these let him pay. A prudent man is free from doubts regarding the sacred law.'

2.9.s: svādhyāyena ṛṣīn pūjya somena ca puraṃdaram | prajayā ca pitqn pūrvān anṛṇo divi modate |
2.9.d: स्वाध्यायेन ऋषीन् पूज्य सोमेन च पुरंदरम् । प्रजया च पित्qन् पूर्वान् अनृणो दिवि मोदते ।
2.9.e: 'If he worships the sages through the study of the Veda, Indra with Soma sacrifices, and the manes of his ancestors through (the procreation of) children, he will rejoice in heaven, free from debt.'

2.9.s: putreṇa lokāñ jayati pautreṇānantyam aśnute | atha putrasya pautreṇa nākam evādhirohati || iti |
2.9.d: पुत्रेण लोकाञ् जयति पौत्रेणानन्त्यम् अश्नुते । अथ पुत्रस्य पौत्रेण नाकम् एवाधिरोहति ॥ इति ।
2.9.e: 'Through a son he conquers the worlds, through a grandson he obtains immortality, but through his son's grandson he ascends to the (highest) heaven.' (All that) has been declared in the Veda.

2.9.s: vijñāyate ca | jāyamāno vai brāhmaṇas tribhir ṛṇavā jāyate brahmacaryeṇarṣibhyo yajñena devebhyaḥ prajayā pitṛbhya iti | evam ṛṇasaṃyogaṃ vedo darśayati |
2.9.d: विज्ञायते च । जायमानो वै ब्राह्मणस् त्रिभिर् ऋणवा जायते ब्रह्मचर्येणर्षिभ्यो यज्ञेन देवेभ्यः प्रजया पितृभ्य इति । एवम् ऋणसंयोगं वेदो दर्शयति ।
2.9.e: The Veda shows the existence of the three debts in the following (passage): 'A Brāhmaṇa is born loaded with three debts; (he owes) the studentship to the sages, sacrifices to the gods, and a son to the manes;'
Through the procreation of a virtuous son he saves himself.

2.9.s: saptāvarān sapta pūrvān ṣaḍ anyān ātmasaptamān | satputram adhigacchānas tārayaty enaso bhayāt |
2.9.d: सप्तावरान् सप्त पूर्वान् षड् अन्यान् आत्मसप्तमान् । सत्पुत्रम् अधिगच्छानस् तारयत्य् एनसो भयात् ।
2.9.e: He who obtains a virtuous son saves from the fear of sin seven in the descending line and seven in the ascending line, (viz.) six others (in each), himself being the seventh.
Therefore he obtains a reward if he begets issue.
Therefore he should sedulously beget offspring,
Through the application of medicines and sacred texts.
The advice to him (who is intent on the procreation of children) is given in agreement with the revealed texts.
For it produces results in the case of all the castes.
